requirements.heading: `.RIP` Stream & File Parsing
requirements.text: [Contents](README.md) · [Next: MegaNum Encoding ▶](1.1-meganum-encoding.md)

requirements.heading: `.RIP` Stream & File Parsing
requirements.text: A `.RIP` file is not a distinct binary format: it is a captured RIPscrip command stream - exactly the bytes a host would transmit - stored as a DOS text file, so everything in the [protocol structure chapter](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md) applies verbatim.

requirements.heading: `.RIP` Stream & File Parsing
requirements.text: _On-disk conventions and spec deviations below are drawn from real 1.5x-era files: RIPaint 1.52's shipped scenes (`~/src/rip-tools/artifacts/ripaint-1.52/RIPAINT.ZIP`) and the RIPtermJS test corpus (`RIPtermJS:rips/`)._

requirements.heading: Storage: CRLF and CP437
requirements.text:
- Line endings are CRLF (`0D 0A`), as in every DOS-era capture examined (e.g. `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP`, hexdump shows `0d 0a` terminators). Line endings are **significant**: a bare CR terminates (dispatches) a command, and parsers treat CR/LF distinctly (see [Parsing model](#parsing-model-stream-not-lines)). This repository stores `.rip` files byte-exact for this reason (`.gitattributes` `-text` exemption; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#checkout--repository-setup)).
- Text content (RIP_TEXT strings, button labels, embedded raw text) is CP437 - the code page of DOS-based BBS terminals and host software. There is no in-band encoding declaration.

requirements.heading: Line structure
requirements.text: Per the spec's syntax rules ([protocol structure](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md), items 1-13):

requirements.heading: Line structure
requirements.text:
- A RIPscrip line begins with `!|` at the start of a line (column 0). Alternatively the `!` may be replaced by SOH (0x01) or STX (0x02), which are allowed mid-line - a host-only capability, since BBS users generally couldn't type control characters (spec item 12; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `cb_accept_introducer()` accepts `!` only at line start but SOH/STX anywhere).
- After the introducer, commands are separated by `|`. Each command is `[level digits][command char][fixed-width meganum args][optional text arg]` - e.g. `!|c0F|L00001010` is two commands (color, line). See [MegaNum Encoding](1.1-meganum-encoding.md) for the numeric fields.
- Anything on a line that does not begin with `!|` (or SOH/STX + `|`) is raw text routed to the text window, including ANSI sequences (spec items 6-7).

requirements.heading: The 80-column convention and `\` continuation
requirements.text: Spec item 5 allows any command or line to be split with a backslash immediately before the line break, "to conform to right margins and escape word wrapping". Observed practice:

requirements.heading: The 80-column convention and `\` continuation
requirements.text:
- TeleGrafix-era tools wrap at 80 columns: every file in `RIPtermJS:rips/set1` and `set2` (RIPaint/RIPterm-era captures) has a maximum line length ≤ 80 including the `\`.
- The split may land **anywhere** - mid-parameter, mid-number, even mid-filename. `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP` line 4 ends `…1A5W1F6A177\` CRLF and resumes with the remainder of the same polygon's coordinate list; another line splits the text `FOR YOUR     VIE\` CRLF `WING PLEASURE…` in the middle of a word.
- The 80-column limit is a writer convention, **not** a reader guarantee: later files in the wild run longer (files in `RIPtermJS:rips/set3` reach 129-130 columns) and terminals accept arbitrarily long lines. Parsers must not allocate fixed 80-byte line buffers.
- Continuation is resolved by counting trailing backslashes: an **odd** count means the last `\` is a continuation (strip it, splice the next line on); an **even** count means the backslashes are escaped literal data and the line ends normally (spec item 13's `\\\` example; implemented in `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `cb_feed()` CR handling).

requirements.heading: Escaping
requirements.text: Inside text parameters (spec items 11 and 13):

requirements.heading: Escaping
requirements.text:
- `\!` → literal `!`, `\|` → literal `|`, `\\` → literal `\`.
- Real-file example: `!|…@1O65FOR YOUR     VIEWING PLEASURE\!|…` in `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP` - the `\!` keeps the exclamation mark out of introducer position; the following `|` still separates commands.
- SyncTERM generalizes: any `\X` other than `\|` collapses to `X` during pre-processing, and `\|` is protected through argument slicing so the pipe reaches the command handler as data (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `cb_unescape()`).

requirements.heading: Parsing model: stream, not lines
requirements.text: Terminals parse `.RIP` content as a byte stream, and files depend on it (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `cb_feed()`/`cb_dispatch()`, whose behavior was verified against RIPterm):

requirements.heading: Parsing model: stream, not lines
requirements.text:
- `|` dispatches the accumulated command immediately and starts the next one - a terminal must not wait for end-of-line to execute.
- CR (not LF) terminates the final command of a line, after the trailing-backslash continuation check; LF is swallowed unconditionally while a command is being accumulated.
- If `!` is not followed by `|`, both characters are re-emitted as ordinary text (un-rip path) - so a lone `!` in column 0 of a text line is safe.
- Unrecognized trailing text after a complete command is ignored without invalidating the command (spec item 6).
- ESC sequences are intercepted by a separate sub-machine even mid-stream, which is how the auto-sense queries work (below).

requirements.heading: Embedded ANSI and plain text
requirements.text: Because non-`!|` lines pass through to the text window, `.RIP` files freely intermix RIPscrip with ANSI. The end of `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP` is a real example - four lines of ANSI music with SGR color and cursor-up sequences sandwiched between RIP lines:

requirements.heading: Embedded ANSI and plain text
requirements.text: The ANSI goes to the text window on top of the graphics; `␛[A` (cursor up) keeps the music lines from scrolling the display. Auto-sensing sequences may also appear in captures: `ESC[!` / `ESC[0!` query the terminal version (answered `RIPSCRIP015410` by RIPterm 1.54), `ESC[1!` disables and `ESC[2!` re-enables RIPscrip parsing ([protocol structure - ANSI sequences](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md#ansi-sequences-auto-sensing); `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `cb_esc_feed()` implements exactly these four).

requirements.heading: Scene prologue and epilogue conventions
requirements.text: TeleGrafix never specified how a `.RIP` file should begin or end, but the shipped scenes are consistent. Surveying first commands across the RIPaint distribution scenes and `RIPtermJS:rips/set1`-`set3`:

requirements.heading: Scene prologue and epilogue conventions
requirements.text:
- **Prologue** - nearly every scene opens with some ordering of: `!|*` ([RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](../ripscrip/1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows) - full reset + clear), `!|1K` ([RIP_KILL_MOUSE_FIELDS](../ripscrip/4.1-mouse-fields.md#rip_kill_mouse_fields) - the spec explicitly recommends it "at the beginning of each Scene"), and a [RIP_TEXT_WINDOW](../ripscrip/1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_text_window) definition (`!|w…`, often `w0000000000` to hide the text window or a full definition like `w0013271410`). Common observed openings: `!|*|1K|w0013271410|…`, `!|1K|*|w0010271610|…`, `!|1K` alone, `!|*` alone.
- Scenes that need a known graphics state continue with `W0` (write mode copy), `=00000001` (solid line, width 1), a palette (`Q…`/`a…`), and a color (`c0F`) before drawing - state is inherited from whatever ran before, so well-behaved scenes re-establish it (cf. [Canvas, Clipping & Write Modes - reset semantics](2.0-canvas-clipping-write-modes.md#reset-semantics)).
- **Epilogue** - files end with `|#|#|#` - three consecutive [RIP_NO_MORE](../ripscrip/5.5-queries-and-advanced-commands.md#rip_no_more) commands, following the spec's own advice that "the Host should transmit three or more RIP_NO_MORE commands consecutively" for noise immunity. Observed at end of file in `11FV.RIP`, `184.RIP`, `MAINMENU.RIP`, and most of the corpus, sometimes followed by one empty CRLF line.

requirements.heading: Known field-layout variance in the wild: RIP_LOAD_ICON `res`
requirements.text: The 1.54 spec defines [RIP_LOAD_ICON](../ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md#rip_load_icon) as `!|1I <x:2> <y:2> <mode:2> <clipboard:1> <res:2> <filename>` and - uniquely among reserved fields - says `res` "should be set to `10`" (`RIPScrip-1.54.txt`, RIP_LOAD_ICON notes). Real 1.5x files disagree with each other:

requirements.heading: Known field-layout variance in the wild: RIP_LOAD_ICON `res`
requirements.text:
```text
RIPAINT.ZIP:MEOW.RIP     !|1I4P2R00110meowbody.ICN     res "10" present (per 1.54 spec)
RIPAINT.ZIP:BOUNCY.RIP   !|1I000003110CHROME.MSK       res "10" present
RIPAINT.ZIP:RIPTANK.RIP  !|1I6Y1X010SHOTU.ICN          res ABSENT (pre-1.54 layout)
RIPAINT.ZIP:RIPTANK.RIP  !|1I002G0101TANK.ICN          res ABSENT (filename "1TANK.ICN")
```

requirements.heading: Known field-layout variance in the wild: RIP_LOAD_ICON `res`
requirements.text: A parser applying the 1.54 field widths to the `RIPTANK.RIP` lines consumes the first two filename characters as `res` (they are valid meganum digits) and then looks for a file that doesn't exist (`OTU.ICN`, `ANK.ICN`). Both styles shipped **in the same RIPaint 1.52 distribution**, so robust loaders of wild files need a heuristic (e.g. try the 1.54 layout, and on file-not-found retry without the `res` field). The spec's odd "set to 10" instruction makes 1.54-conformant streams self-consistent - but nothing enforces it in older material. This is the sharpest known example of why `.RIP` archives cannot be parsed by field widths alone without version context.

requirements.heading: Related: local playback
requirements.text: RIPterm can replay local `.RIP` files outside a connection: the `-R<file>` command-line switch, and the `$>FILENAME$` [local playback text variables](../ripscrip/5.3-local-playback.md) (e.g. `$>FILE1.RIP$$>FILE2.RIP$`), which search the current host's icon directory then `ICONS\` (RIPTERM.DOC, "-R" startup option and §on local RIP playback variables; the lookup order is part of the [connection directory model](4.0-connection-directory-model.md)). [RIP_PLAY_MACRO / scene playback](../ripscrip/5.5-queries-and-advanced-commands.md) likewise feeds a cached file back through the same stream parser (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `rip_play_scene()` re-enters `cb_feed()` with saved parser state, recursion capped at 8 levels).

requirements.heading: Related: local playback
requirements.text: [Contents](README.md) · [Next: MegaNum Encoding ▶](1.1-meganum-encoding.md)

requirements.heading: MegaNum Encoding
requirements.text: RIPscrip's numeric parameters are base-36 ("Hexa-Tri-Decimal", dubbed **MegaNums**), using digits `0`-`9` and `A`-`Z`, most significant digit first, in fixed-width fields with no delimiters (spec, [protocol structure](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md) item 10). The spec defines the digit set and per-command field widths but leaves signedness, case, invalid input, and overflow behavior unstated.

requirements.heading: Basics
requirements.text:
- Digit values: `0`-`9` = 0-9, `A`-`Z` = 10-35. Value = Σ digit·36^position, MSD first: `2G` = 2·36 + 16 = 88.
- Fields are fixed-width and zero-padded; writers emit uppercase (all TeleGrafix-authored files observed use uppercase only, e.g. every scene in `~/src/rip-tools/artifacts/ripaint-1.52/RIPAINT.ZIP` and `RIPtermJS:rips/`).
- Ranges per width: 1 digit 0-35, 2 digits 0-1,295, 3 digits 0-46,655, 4 digits 0-1,679,615, 6 digits 0-2,176,782,335. Screen coordinates use width 2 (1,295 comfortably covers 0-639).
- If a command takes a text string, it is always the **last** parameter and is never meganum-encoded; a variable-width numeric parameter may also appear last (spec item 10) - in practice this is the coordinate list of the polygon/polyline commands (`P`, `p`, `l`), a repeated sequence of 2-digit pairs running to end of command.

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: Widths are defined per parameter in each command's spec entry (see the [command reference](../ripscrip/9.0-command-reference.md) and the per-chapter pages - e.g. RIP_TEXT_XY `@` is `x:2, y:2, text`, RIP_LINE_STYLE `=` is `style:2, user_pat:4, thick:2`, RIP_BUTTON_STYLE `1B` ends with a 6-digit `flags2`-era field). SyncTERM encodes the full width map as descriptor strings - `2#` = 2-digit field, `+2#` = variable-length list of 2-digit fields, `++` = trailing text - in its `rip_cmd_descs[]` table (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c`), which is a convenient machine-readable cross-check of every 1.5x command's layout. Notable widths beyond the ubiquitous `2#`:

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: | Command | Descriptor | Reading |

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: | RIP_LINE_STYLE `=` | `2#4#2#` | style, 16-bit user pattern as 4 digits, thickness |

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: | RIP_FILL_PATTERN `s` | `2#` ×9 | eight 8-bit pattern rows + fill color, each 2 digits |

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: | RIP_WRITE_MODE `W` | `1#` | single digit 0/1 |

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: | RIP_FONT_STYLE `Y` | `2#2#2#1#1#` | font, direction, size, then the reserved word split 1+1 |

requirements.heading: Field widths
requirements.text: | RIP_POLYGON `P` / RIP_POLYLINE `l` | `2#2#2#+2#` | npoints, first x, first y, then 2-digit pairs to end |

requirements.heading: Edge cases as implemented
requirements.text: The subtleties below matter for byte-exact compatibility with RIPterm and with wild `.RIP` data. Primary source: SyncTERM's parser, whose comment declares it "BGI-exact" - i.e. matched to RIPterm's observed behavior (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `parse_mega()`); cross-checked against `icy_tools:crates/icy_parser_core/src/rip/builder.rs` (`BASE36_LUT`, `parse_base36_complete()`), `RIPtermJS:src/ripterm.js` (`parseRIPargs()`), and `pablodraw:Source/Pablo/Formats/Rip/RipExtensions.cs` (`ReadRipNumber()`/`ReadRipWord()`).

requirements.heading: Edge cases as implemented
requirements.text:
- **Case-insensitive digits.** `a`-`z` are accepted with the same values as `A`-`Z` (`parse_mega()`: explicit `'a'..'z'` branch; `BASE36_LUT` maps both ranges). Writers still emit uppercase; lowercase appears in the wild in filenames-adjacent contexts (e.g. `meowbody.ICN` follows lowercase-tolerant fields in `RIPAINT.ZIP:MEOW.RIP`). PabloDraw is the outlier: it accepts only `0-9A-Z` and silently reads any other byte as digit value 0 (`ReadRipNumber()` returns 0 on fall-through).
- **MegaNums are unsigned; `-` is not a sign.** No 1.54 parameter is negative. SyncTERM's BGI-exact parser accepts `-` **as a digit with value 0** (`ret = ret * 36`), so `-5` parses as 5 and `1-` as 36 - quirk compatibility, not signedness. No writer emits `-`.
- **Early termination.** A field may be cut short by `|` (next command) or end-of-input after at least one digit; the value is whatever was accumulated (`parse_mega()`: `break` on `'|'`/`'\0'` when `i > 0`). Wild files depend on this: `!|W0|…` (1 digit for the spec's 2-digit write mode) appears in the opening line of `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP`.
- **Invalid characters reject the whole command.** Any other byte inside a numeric field makes the command fail: SyncTERM returns -1 and the command is dropped; RIPtermJS gets `NaN` from `parseInt(…, 36)` and skips the command (`noNaNs()` guard). For variable-length coordinate lists, SyncTERM additionally rejects the entire command if non-meganum bytes remain after the list (`parse_rip_args()` comment: "BGI rejects the entire command if any non-meganum characters remain after the varlen fields").
- **No overflow checking.** Accumulation is unchecked multiply-add; icy_term wraps at 16 bits (`wrapping_mul`/`wrapping_add` into `u16`), SyncTERM accumulates into a C `int`. Well-formed 1.54 traffic never exceeds 16-bit values except in the 6-digit button-style field.
- **Splitting across continuations.** Because line continuation is handled below the tokenizer, a fixed-width field can be split by `\` CRLF mid-number (observed in `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP`; PabloDraw reads through continuations inside `ReadRipByte()` before digit conversion). See [.RIP Stream & File Parsing](1.0-rip-stream-parsing.md#the-80-column-convention-and--continuation).
- **Composition in decoders.** Multi-digit fields are just positional accumulation - PabloDraw expresses a 2-digit word as `ReadRipNumber() * 36 + ReadRipNumber()` and a 4-digit int as `word * 1296 + word` (`RipExtensions.cs`), a useful identity for writers: emit `value / 36^k % 36` per position.

requirements.heading: Canvas, Clipping & Write Modes
requirements.text: Pixel-level semantics the 1.54 specification leaves unstated: what exactly XOR mode XORs, what happens when an icon crosses the viewport edge, which state a reset actually clears.

requirements.heading: Canvas, Clipping & Write Modes
requirements.text: _Reconstructed from the reference implementations - chiefly `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c`, annotated with behaviors "verified against RIPterm", and `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js`, a from-scratch BGI reimplementation tested against RIPterm 1.54 output. Where a behavior is one implementation's choice rather than verified RIPterm behavior, it is marked as such._

requirements.heading: Screen model
requirements.text:
- The drawing surface is 640x350, 16 colors out of the EGA 64-color master palette (spec, [RIP_VIEWPORT](../ripscrip/1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_viewport): "Coordinates are specified based on a 640x350 pixel resolution"; RIPterm links Borland's EGAVGA driver - see [BGI Stroked Fonts](3.1-bgi-stroked-fonts.md#egavgabgi-and-the-rendering-pipeline)).
- EGA pixels are non-square (640x350 on a 4:3 display); handling of that is a renderer policy decision, documented in [implementation.md](../../implementation.md).
- Colors are palette **indices**; all raster-op semantics below operate on the 4-bit index, never on RGB values.

requirements.heading: Viewport clipping and coordinates
requirements.text:
- All graphics output is clipped ("truncated") to the RIP_VIEWPORT rectangle; the spec states this only in the RIP_VIEWPORT entry, but it applies to every drawing primitive, including text and image stamps.
- Drawing coordinates are **viewport-relative**: pixel (x, y) lands at screen (viewport.x0 + x, viewport.y0 + y) (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `draw_pixel()`/`set_pixel()` add `rip.viewport.sx/sy` and clip against the viewport extent).
- An all-zero viewport (`!|v00000000`) disables graphics output entirely - commands are parsed but draw nothing (spec: "The viewport may be disabled ... by setting all parameters to zero"; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `no_viewport()` guards the drawing paths).
- Bitmap-font text has a per-character clipping quirk: rather than clipping a glyph pixel-by-pixel at the right/bottom viewport edge, RIPterm skips the **entire character** when its cell would cross the edge, while still advancing the text position - SyncTERM reproduces this with a clip extent of `8·size - 2` (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `write_char()`, "Per-character viewport clipping" comment).

requirements.heading: Write modes (RIP_WRITE_MODE)
requirements.text: [RIP_WRITE_MODE](../ripscrip/2.0-colors-and-attributes.md#rip_write_mode) `!|W <mode:2>`: mode 00 = copy (overwrite), mode 01 = XOR. Real files often send just one digit (`!|W0` appears in the opening line of `RIPtermJS:rips/set1/11FV.RIP`), relying on [meganum early termination](1.1-meganum-encoding.md#edge-cases-as-implemented) at the `|`; SyncTERM's descriptor table even declares the field 1-digit (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `rip_cmd_descs[]` entry `{0, 'W', "1#"}`). Under-specified detail:

requirements.heading: Write modes (RIP_WRITE_MODE)
requirements.text:
- XOR combines the current drawing color's **palette index** with the **palette index of the pixel already on screen**: `new_index = old_index ^ draw_color_index` (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `draw_pixel()`: reads the pixel back, maps it to its palette slot via `pixel2color()`, XORs, rewrites). With a modified palette this is very different from XORing RGB.
- Write mode affects lines, rectangles, polygons/polylines, Beziers, and graphics text (per the spec's per-command attribute matrix; circles/ovals/arcs/pie slices, bars, pixels, and flood fills are marked `Uses Write Mode: NO`); drawing the same figure twice in XOR mode restores the original screen - the spec relies on this for animation (its Bezier notes describe erase-by-redraw, `RIPScrip-1.54.txt` RIP_BEZIER section; SyncTERM's comments around the mouse-region inverter make the same point).
- Icon/clipboard stamping ignores RIP_WRITE_MODE - it has its own mode parameter (below).

requirements.heading: Image put modes (RIP_PUT_IMAGE / RIP_LOAD_ICON)
requirements.text:
- AND+OR pairs implement transparency via `.MSK` files - see [Icon Format](3.0-icon-format.md#msk-mask-files) for the observed mask convention.
- **Off-edge icons are refused, not clipped.** If any part of the icon would extend past the viewport's right or bottom edge, RIP_LOAD_ICON draws nothing at all (spec: "If the width or height of the Icon would make it go off the right or left edge of the screen, the Icon will not be displayed"; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `load_stamp_icon()` rejects before drawing; `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `putimage()` logs "ignored: right edge past canvas edge"). This differs from every other primitive, which clips.
- **No icon scaling exists in 1.5x.** Icons and clipboard images are stamped 1:1 device pixels; there is no zoom/stretch command in the 1.54 command set, and the only "magnification" anywhere in the system is font-size pixel replication ([RIP_FONT_STYLE](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_font_style)). Modern renderers that scale output do so on the whole 640x350 framebuffer, not per icon (SyncTERM's `scale_setpixel`; see [implementation.md](../../implementation.md)).

requirements.heading: "Image too large" side effects
requirements.text: A BGI image buffer is limited to 65,535 bytes (16-bit `imagesize()`), i.e. `⌈w/8⌉·4·h + 6 ≤ 65535`. RIPterm reacts to an over-limit RIP_GET_IMAGE/RIP_LOAD_ICON with an "Image too large" error popup - and the popup itself **clobbers graphics state**: afterward, draw color = 7, fill color = 8, fill style = solid, line width = 1, line style = solid, write mode = copy. SyncTERM replicates these side effects, noting they were "empirically verified by setting known state before triggering the popup and checking each variable after" (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `bgi_imagesize_ok()` / `rip_image_too_large()`). Scenes that trip the limit therefore corrupt subsequent drawing state on a real RIPterm.

requirements.heading: Fonts and text
requirements.text:
- Stroked-font sizes are **not** linear magnifications: RIP size 4 is 1:1, size 1 is 60% (full ratio table and citations in [BGI Stroked Fonts](3.1-bgi-stroked-fonts.md#scaling-rip-size-vs-actual-magnification)). The spec's "01 for the normal default size, 02 for x2..." sentence is accurate only for bitmap font 0, whose magnification is N× pixel replication ([Bitmap Fonts](3.2-bitmap-fonts.md#rip_font_style-font-0---the-default-8x8-graphics-font)).
- Graphics text (all fonts) is drawn with the current drawing color and honors XOR write mode; stroked glyphs are stroked as solid 1-px vectors regardless of line style ([BGI Stroked Fonts](3.1-bgi-stroked-fonts.md#egavgabgi-and-the-rendering-pipeline)).
- Vertical direction (01) rotates glyphs 90° counter-clockwise; the current position advances only along the writing direction (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `write_char()`; `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `drawChar()` direction handling).
- Text width must be computed as sum-of-unscaled-widths, then scaled once (not per-glyph), to match RIPterm's rounding (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `textwidth()` "sum-then-scale" comment).

requirements.heading: Reset semantics
requirements.text: What [RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](../ripscrip/1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows) `!|*` does (spec + implementation-verified additions):

requirements.heading: Reset semantics
requirements.text:
- Per spec: full-screen text window (80x43) and graphics viewport (640x350), clear screen, home cursor, kill all mouse regions/buttons, erase clipboard, restore the default 16-color palette.
- Verified additions and omissions (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` reset path): the border/cursor/hotkey states reset, **but line pattern and line width survive** the reset (comment: "verified against RIPterm reference implementation"; see [line styles and patterns](2.1-pattern-fill-rasterization.md#line-styles-and-patterns)). Well-behaved scenes therefore re-send `!|=…` after `!|*` - and the shipped TeleGrafix scenes do exactly that (see [scene prologue conventions](1.0-rip-stream-parsing.md#scene-prologue-and-epilogue-conventions)).
- Draw color, fill state, write mode, and font state also persist from scene to scene unless explicitly reset; there is no "reset all attributes" command in 1.54.

requirements.heading: Mouse regions
requirements.text:
- At most 128 mouse fields + buttons combined may exist; hit-testing scans **most recent first**, so overlapping regions resolve to the newest.
- Region/button inversion feedback ("visibly inverted while the mouse button is down", spec [RIP_MOUSE](../ripscrip/4.1-mouse-fields.md#rip_mouse) `<clk>` flag) complements each on-screen pixel's palette index: `index ^ 0x0F` (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `invert_rect()`; button color inversion likewise uses `0x0f ^ color` throughout `draw_button()`).

requirements.heading: Line styles and patterns
requirements.text: [RIP_LINE_STYLE](../ripscrip/2.1-lines.md#rip_line_style) `!|= <style:2> <user_pat:4> <thick:2>`:

requirements.heading: Line styles and patterns
requirements.text:
- The four predefined styles are 16-bit patterns: solid `FFFF`, dotted `CCCC`, centered `FC78`, dashed `F8F8`; style 04 uses the 4-digit user pattern verbatim (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `rip_line_patterns[4]`; pattern values match the spec's style descriptions).
- **One pattern bit is consumed per pixel** along the line, cycling through the 16 bits; a set bit draws the pixel, a clear bit skips it (leaves the screen untouched - patterned lines are transparent in the gaps, not background-colored). SyncTERM advances the bit position `pp = (pp + 1) & 0x0F` and tests `pattern & (1 << pp)`, i.e. LSB first (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `draw_line_to()`).
- The pattern position **carries across the segments of a connected figure** (polyline/polygon/Bezier joints continue the cycle rather than restarting it) - `draw_line_to()` threads the position through by pointer.
- Thickness is 1 or 3 only (spec). A thick line is drawn as three 1-pixel lines: the center line plus offsets of ±1 perpendicular to the line's major axis, each independently clipped, matching BGI (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `draw_line_to()` width-3 branch and its comment).
- Line patterns apply to lines, polylines, polygons, and Beziers. Rectangle outlines also honor them; circles/ellipses/arcs in BGI ignore the line _pattern_ (they draw solid) though the thickness applies - 1.54 scenes rarely exercise this corner; treat it as BGI-inherited behavior. The spec explicitly recommends patterned Beziers for special effects and warns about XOR redraw for animation (`RIPScrip-1.54.txt` RIP_BEZIER notes).
- **RIP_RESET_WINDOWS does not reset line pattern or line width** - "(verified against RIPterm reference implementation)" (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c`, comment in the reset path). See [Reset semantics](2.0-canvas-clipping-write-modes.md#reset-semantics).

requirements.heading: Fill styles and patterns
requirements.text: [RIP_FILL_STYLE](../ripscrip/2.3-shapes-and-fills.md#rip_fill_style) selects one of 12 patterns (00 background … 11 close-dot) plus a fill color; [RIP_FILL_PATTERN](../ripscrip/2.3-shapes-and-fills.md#rip_fill_pattern) sets a user-defined 8x8 pattern (eight 2-digit rows, top row first, bit 7 = leftmost pixel) and the fill color.

requirements.heading: Fill styles and patterns
requirements.text:
- **Two-color rendering, not transparency:** for every filled pixel, a set pattern bit paints the current **fill color** and a clear bit paints **color 0 (black)** - not the "background color" state and not transparent (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `native_fill_pixel()`: `fill_pattern[y & 7] & (0x80 >> (x & 7)) ? fill_color : color 0`).
- **Patterns are anchored to absolute screen coordinates** (`x & 7`, `y & 7` of the device pixel), so adjacent filled shapes tile seamlessly and a shape refilled at the same position aligns with itself (`native_fill_pixel()` operates on post-viewport screen coordinates).
- Fill style 00 ("background fill"): SyncTERM's scanline polygon filler simply skips filling entirely when style 0 is active (`scanline_poly_fill()` step 1: "Skip if fill_style == 0"). Since the pattern for style 0 is all-zero bits, painting it would produce solid black; skipping produces nothing. Which of the two RIPterm 1.54 actually did for filled _polygons_ is unverified; for bars/flood fills an all-zero pattern paints solid color-0 by the rule above.
- Filled primitives (RIP_BAR, RIP_FILLED_POLYGON, pie slices, flood fill) fill with the pattern; the _outline_, where the primitive has one, is drawn separately with the current drawing color and line state.
- Filled-polygon rasterization is scanline even-odd with **inclusive** spans between sorted edge intersections, edges treated as half-open in y (`y_min ≤ y < y_max`) so shared vertices don't double-count (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `scanline_poly_fill()` - algorithm annotated as "matching RIPterm's algorithm").
- The spec's own pattern table contains an error RIPterm faithfully implements: the "Light Backslash" style's documented bytes (`A5 D2 69 B4 5A 2D 96 4B`) do not form a backslash pattern (the plausible intended bytes `80 40 20 10 08 04 02 01` do). SyncTERM ships the documented bytes, labeling the alternative "as expected" and the shipped one "as documented" (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `rip_fill_patterns[12]`). Match the documented bytes for fidelity.
- [RIP_FILL](../ripscrip/2.3-shapes-and-fills.md#rip_fill) (flood fill) fills the connected region at (x, y) bounded by pixels of the given **border color**, using the current fill pattern/color; the border pixels themselves are untouched, and if the border does not fully enclose the seed point the fill spreads to the viewport edges (spec, RIP_FILL notes). In Borland's `floodfill()`, seeding on a pixel that is already the border color does nothing; this is inherited BGI behavior (unverified against RIPterm itself).

requirements.heading: Icon Format (`.ICN` / `.MSK` / `.HIC`)
requirements.text: A RIPscrip icon is a device-dependent 16-color bitmap in Borland BGI `getimage()`/`putimage()` buffer format, written to disk verbatim; `.ICN` (icons), `.MSK` (masks) and `.HIC` (hot icons) are the identical format, distinguished only by role. The 1.54 specification documents it in its [appendix](../ripscrip/6.1-content-file-roles.md) (`RIPScrip-1.54.txt`, "APPENDIX A: RIPscrip ICON FILE FORMAT SPECIFICATION"), whose trailing-byte count does not match the files RIPterm and RIPaint actually shipped.

The inherited binary layout is tested independently for v3 conversion; these observations do not require modifying the frozen 1.54 implementation or infer the unverified 2.x/3.x BMM convention. V3 automatic conversion and palette/filesystem policy are tracked separately.

requirements.heading: Binary layout
requirements.text:
- Each plane chunk is one monochrome row: ⌈width/8⌉ bytes, bit 7 of each byte = leftmost pixel, rows padded on the right with don't-care bits (spec appendix).
- A pixel's 4-bit color index is assembled as `(plane3_bit << 3) | (plane2_bit << 2) | (plane1_bit << 1) | plane0_bit` - i.e. the file stores plane 3 (bit 3) first (spec appendix worked example; `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `fetchIcon()`; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `load_stamp_icon()` plane-unpacking loop).
- The color indices are standard EGA palette slots 0-15 as set by RIP_SET_PALETTE; icons carry no palette of their own. This does not choose an RGB palette for later conversion: the original RIPtel 3.1 converter writes a [fixed EGA BMP color table](../../3.0/techspecs/3.0-bitmap-mask-delta.md#legacy-icon-conversion-palette), regardless of that client’s current drawing palette. This later-client observation does not change the 1.54 raster definition.

requirements.heading: File size and the trailing bytes
requirements.text: **The spec appendix is wrong about the tail.** [The appendix](../ripscrip/6.1-content-file-roles.md) documents exactly **one** trailing "trash byte", and its worked example (6x2 image) totals 13 bytes; real files always carry **two** trailing bytes. The values are garbage - observed tails include `00 00` (`WORLD-1.ICN`), `01 00` (`BUBBLE.MSK`), `04 00` (`BUTTON.ICN`), `39 3a` (`MOUSE.ICN`) - consistent with RIPterm writing the full uninitialized `imagesize()` buffer that Borland's EGAVGA driver allocates, whose size is data + 6 bytes (4 header + 2 slack). SyncTERM encodes the same 6-byte overhead in its size-limit check: `imgsz = ((w + 7) / 8) * 4 * h + 6` (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c`, `bgi_imagesize_ok()`). Readers should simply ignore everything after the pixel data; writers wanting byte-exact fidelity with TeleGrafix tools should emit two zero bytes.
requirements.reason: The legacy icon reader and RADIO.ICN conversion fixture cover the little-endian size header, plane order, row padding and ignored tail.

requirements.heading: File size and the trailing bytes
requirements.text: Because the BGI buffer size is a 16-bit quantity, an icon whose buffer would exceed 65,535 bytes cannot exist as a valid BGI image; RIPterm reacts to over-size images with an "Image too large" error popup that has observable side effects on the drawing state (see [Canvas, Clipping & Write Modes](2.0-canvas-clipping-write-modes.md#image-too-large-side-effects)).

requirements.heading: How icons are referenced and stored
requirements.text:
- RIPTERM.DOC's glossary defines the three extensions together: "an icon is a bit map graphic of varying size. Icon files may end in .ICN, .MSK (mask files), or .HIC (hot icons - used with buttons)" (`~/src/rip-tools/RIPterm154/DOS/RIPTERM/RIPTERM.DOC`, §1.7 glossary).
- Icon files live in the `ICONS\` sub-directory of the RIPterm install, optionally in per-host sub-directories falling back to `ICONS\` (RIPTERM.DOC §1.5 and the host-directory notes around its "icons" configuration field) - the storage layout and lookup order are documented in [Connection Directory Model](4.0-connection-directory-model.md).
- [RIP_LOAD_ICON](../ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md#rip_load_icon) filenames may not contain path information; if the filename has no extension, `.ICN` is appended, and an explicit extension (e.g. `.MSK`) is used verbatim (spec; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `load_stamp_icon()` rejects `/`, `\`, `..` and appends `.ICN` only when the name has no `.`).
- [RIP_WRITE_ICON](../ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md#rip_write_icon) writes the clipboard to disk in this same format; [RIP_GET_IMAGE](../ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md#rip_get_image)/[RIP_PUT_IMAGE](../ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md#rip_put_image) use the identical buffer in memory.

requirements.heading: `.MSK` mask files
requirements.text: A `.MSK` file is structurally an ordinary icon whose four bit planes are **identical**, so every pixel is either color 0 (black) or color 15 (white). Verified programmatically for all four masks shipped with RIPterm 1.54 (`BUBBLE.MSK` 27x23, `CHROME.MSK` 47x34, `MOUSE.MSK` 97x36, `TANK.MSK` 129x56 in `~/src/rip-tools/RIPterm154/DOS/RIPTERM/ICONS/`): in each file, planes 0-2 of every scan line are byte-identical to plane 3.

requirements.heading: `.MSK` mask files
requirements.text:
- RIPaint's help topic "Icon Mask Creation" describes authoring: the icon editor's Mask button converts the image to black and white (the chosen "invisible" color and any black pixels become the mask), saved with the icon's basename and an `.MSK` extension; "When you load this mask image first before you load the original icon in the same spot, the color you selected to be invisible will not show up" (`RIPAINT.HLP` in `~/src/rip-tools/artifacts/ripaint-1.52/RIPAINT.ZIP`).
- Observed in shipped scenes: RIPaint's `BOUNCY.RIP` animates a ball with repeated pairs `!|1I000003110CHROME.MSK` (mode 03 = AND) immediately followed by `!|1I000002110CHROME.ICN` (mode 02 = OR) at the same coordinates (`RIPAINT.ZIP:BOUNCY.RIP`).

requirements.heading: BGI Stroked Fonts (`.CHR`)
requirements.text: RIPscrip's scalable fonts 1-10 are Borland Graphics Interface (BGI) **stroked fonts**: each glyph is a sequence of move/draw vector strokes, scaled at render time, in the same format as Borland's BGI Toolkit (1987-89).
requirements.reason: The CHR decoder reads the stroke tables and maps the ten numbered faces. The classic text path scales and draws the resulting strokes.

requirements.heading: File structure
requirements.text: A `.CHR` file has three parts: a text prefix header, a binary stroke-file header, and the glyph tables/stroke data.
requirements.reason: The CHR decoder reads the stroke tables and maps the ten numbered faces. The classic text path scales and draws the resulting strokes.

requirements.heading: Prefix header (offset 0)
requirements.text:
```text
offset 0:      "PK\b\b"                       4-byte signature (50 4B 08 08)
offset 4:      description text               e.g. "BGI Stroked Font V1.1 - Jun 5, 1989\r\n
                                              Copyright (c) 1987,1988 Borland International\r\n"
               0x1A                           DOS EOF byte terminates the text
EOF+1:         uint16 header_size             offset of the stroke-file header (0x0080 in all shipped files)
EOF+3:         char   font_name[4]            internal name: "TRIP", "LITT", ...
EOF+7:         uint16 font_data_size          size of everything from header_size to end of file
EOF+9:         uint8  version_major, version_minor      driver version (1, 0 in all shipped files)
EOF+11:        uint8  min_version_major, min_version_minor   minimum BGI revision (1, 0)
               zero padding up to header_size
```
requirements.reason: The CHR decoder reads the stroke tables and maps the ten numbered faces. The classic text path scales and draws the resulting strokes.

requirements.heading: Prefix header (offset 0)
requirements.text: Verified against `../../1.54/assets/fonts/TRIP.CHR`: bytes at the 0x1A terminator read `1a 80 00 54 52 49 50 a5 40 01 00 01 00` - header size 0x0080, name `TRIP`, data size 0x40A5 = 16,549, and 128 + 16,549 = 16,677 = the exact file size. The `header_size + font_data_size = file_size` identity holds for all ten shipped fonts (decoded programmatically; see the table below).
requirements.reason: Inventory and measurements of the shipped 1.54 assets and driver. Glyph decoding and selection have separate requirements.

requirements.heading: Stroke-file header (offset `header_size`, 16 bytes)
requirements.text:
```c
struct chr_stroke_header {          /* at offset 0x80 in all shipped files */
    char     sig;                   /* '+' (0x2B) marks a stroke font      */
    uint16_t nchars;                /* number of glyphs in the font        */
    char     undefined;
    uint8_t  firstchar;             /* ASCII code of the first glyph       */
    uint16_t cdefs;                 /* offset of stroke data, relative to
                                       the stroke-file header              */
    uint8_t  scan_flag;             /* 0 in all shipped files              */
    int8_t   org_to_cap;            /* baseline to capital top (px, up +)  */
    int8_t   org_to_base;           /* baseline offset (0 in all files)    */
    int8_t   org_to_dec;            /* baseline to descender bottom (neg.) */
    char     name[4];               /* unused; not required to be zero      */
    char     unused;
};
```

requirements.heading: Stroke-file header (offset `header_size`, 16 bytes)
requirements.text: **Observed-byte correction:** the unused `name[4]` field is not uniformly zero. TSCR.CHR contains **02 03 00 00** at stroke-header +11..+14 (file **0x8B..0x8E**). Its internal font name still comes from the prefix header; no meaning is assigned here to these unused bytes. The byte-exact TSCR payload has SHA-256 `305e2a9657902fef2a52b25e398a5e2fca4cd0ace0fc0208704b2cb5c360b187` and is pinned identically in the 1.54 and 3.0 asset trees. _Evidence: original file and [hash/header census](../../3.0/research/issue-17-chr-scan-records.md#recovered-bytes-and-census)._

requirements.heading: Stroke opcodes
requirements.text:
- For MOVE/DRAW: x = byte 1 & 0x7F, y = byte 2 & 0x7F, both sign-extended from 7 bits.
- Coordinates are absolute within the glyph, relative to the glyph origin at the **baseline** left edge, with **y positive upward** (Borland convention; renderers negate y for screen space - `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `drawChar()` computes `y = y0 - dy`; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `write_char()` likewise subtracts the y stroke term).
- Decoder evidence: `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `fetchCHRFont()`/`drawChar()`; `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `write_char()`.

requirements.heading: SCAN records and RIPtel rendering
requirements.text: Every one is followed by MOVE. The other nine RIPtel CHR files contain no SCAN records reached through their glyph tables. This census preserves the raw opcode; it does not reinterpret it as a MOVE or END.

requirements.heading: SCAN records and RIPtel rendering
requirements.text: **RIPtel 3.1 / RIPscrip driver 3.0.7 painting contract:** consume the two SCAN bytes and continue to the next record in the same glyph. SCAN paints nothing and leaves pen position, contour state and advance unchanged. It does not fill or scan-convert a preceding closed region, add a closing edge, connect contours, flush strokes or terminate the glyph. Its low seven-bit payload values are ignored. The original horizontal and vertical glyph loops branch only for END/MOVE/DRAW; SCAN takes the default continuation path. This is original-client evidence, separate from a peer decoder's IGNORE choice, and does not claim a runtime result for earlier Borland/RIPterm clients.
requirements.reason: The decoder consumes the two-byte SCAN record. The renderer skips the record, preserving the previous DRAW endpoint with a nonzero payload and scan_flag. Live BOLD text covers all five affected glyphs and the complete string advance.

requirements.heading: SCAN records and RIPtel rendering
requirements.text: `scan_flag` is **0 in all ten RIPtel fonts**. RIPtel's original classic loader and glyph consumer do not use it to enable scanning or filling. Setting it to any other byte value before loading leaves these glyphs' drawing and state unchanged. Thus these records are no-ops regardless of that flag, rather than active scan operations suppressed specifically by zero.

requirements.heading: Scaling: RIP size vs. actual magnification
requirements.text: RIP_FONT_STYLE's `<size>` parameter (01-0A) is passed straight through to BGI's `settextstyle()` charsize, and BGI charsize is **not** a linear multiplier. The spec's claim that "01 [is] the normal default size, 02 for x2 magnification, … 0A for x10" is only true of bitmap font 0; for stroked fonts the real factors are Borland's charsize ratios, with **size 4 being 1:1 stroke units**:

requirements.heading: `EGAVGA.BGI` and the rendering pipeline
requirements.text: RIPterm 1.54 does **not** ship any `.BGI` driver file - the RIPTERM.DOC distribution file list contains only the `.CHR` fonts and `RIPTERM.FNT`. The Borland EGA/VGA display driver is linked into the executable: `RIPTERM.EXE` embeds the strings `BGI Device Driver (EGAVGA) 2.00 - Mar 21 1988` and `Copyright (c) 1987,1988 Borland International` (observed via `strings` on `~/src/rip-tools/RIPterm154/DOS/RIPTERM/RIPTERM.EXE`), i.e. EGAVGA.BGI converted with Borland's `BGIOBJ` and registered at link time. RIPterm runs the driver's 640x350x16 EGAHI mode, which is why RIPscrip 1.54 coordinates are 640x350 (`RIPScrip-1.54.txt`: "Coordinates are specified based on a 640x350 pixel resolution").
requirements.reason: Inventory and measurements of the shipped 1.54 assets and driver. Glyph decoding and selection have separate requirements.

requirements.heading: `EGAVGA.BGI` and the rendering pipeline
requirements.text:
- Stroked text is drawn as vectors through the same line-drawing state machine as everything else, but always with solid 1-pixel lines regardless of the current line style; only the current drawing color and write mode apply (`RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `drawChar()` calls `lineto(..., SOLID_LINE, NORM_WIDTH)`; see [Canvas, Clipping & Write Modes](2.0-canvas-clipping-write-modes.md) for write-mode details).
- Glyph metrics, kerning (none - pure advance widths), and scaling must reproduce BGI's integer arithmetic to match RIPterm pixel-for-pixel.

requirements.text: Consistency proof: each charset size equals **255 × bytes_per_glyph**, consecutive offsets differ by exactly that amount, and 11,456 + 7,140 = 18,596 - the file size to the byte. Header + directory = 26 + 5·42 = 236 = the first data offset, so the file is fully accounted for with no gaps.

requirements.heading: Glyph data
requirements.text:
- Each charset stores **255 glyphs for character codes 1-255**; code 0 is not stored (glyph index = code - 1). Evidence: the first glyph at offset 236 is `7e 81 a5 81 bd 99 81 7e` - the classic IBM 8x8 smiley, CP437 code point 1 - and indexing `'A'` (0x41) at offset 236 + 0x40·8 yields `38 6c c6 c6 fe c6 c6 00`, the standard 8x8 capital A.
- Rows are stored top to bottom, one row per `ceil(width/8)` bytes, bit 7 = leftmost pixel; the 7-wide charsets still use one byte per row (low bit unused), and the 16-wide charset stores two bytes per row, left byte first.
- The glyph repertoire is CP437, the IBM PC code page used by DOS-based BBS terminals (box-drawing, block, and dingbat characters render correctly when decoded per the layout above).

Behavior details, as specified and as implemented:
requirements.reason: Historical RIPterm bitmap-font container and defaults. The RIPv3 MAF and outline-font requirements are reviewed separately.

requirements.heading: RIP_FONT_STYLE font 0 - the default 8x8 graphics font
requirements.text:
- **Magnification is pixel replication.** At size N each glyph pixel becomes an N×N block and the character cell advances 8·N pixels; the spec itself warns the result looks jagged above size 1 (spec note under RIP_FONT_STYLE; implementation: `sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `write_char()` replicates each set bit over `size × size` pixels, `RIPtermJS:src/BGI.js` `drawPNGChar()` scales the same way). Unlike the stroked fonts, size 1 really is 1:1 for font 0 - see the scaling-table discrepancy in [BGI Stroked Fonts](3.1-bgi-stroked-fonts.md#scaling-rip-size-vs-actual-magnification).
- **Both directions are supported.** Direction 01 (vertical) rotates each glyph 90° counter-clockwise and advances upward, matching stroked-font behavior (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `write_char()` vertical branch).
- **Text drawn with font 0 honors the current drawing color and write mode**, like all graphics text ([RIP_TEXT attributes list](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_text): "Draw Color, Write Mode, Font Sizes, Viewport").
- **Full 1-255 repertoire.** Because the charset covers codes 1-255, font 0 can draw CP437 line/block art in the graphics window (subject to the [protocol's escaping rules](1.0-rip-stream-parsing.md#escaping) for `!`, `|`, `\`).

requirements.heading: The two directories
requirements.text:
- **Connection directory** - a per-host (per-connection) asset directory associated with each dialing-directory entry (RIPterm's DIR field; a bookmark/profile field in a modern client). RIPTERM.DOC: "Each entry in the directory has the ability to have a separate sub-directory associated with it. This is used mainly when RIPscrip graphics are being viewed on the host. Any icon (.ICN, .MSK, .HIC) or RIPscrip (.RIP) files that are received by the host [sic - from the host] should be placed in the designated sub-directory. This in effect, helps keep your icons separated from each other."
- **Default icon directory** - the shared fallback directory, historically `ICONS\` under the client install. RIPTERM.DOC: "If you omit a directory name in this field, and you dial into a RIPscrip host that requires icons or RIPscrip files, RIPterm will look for them automatically in the ICONS\ sub-directory." It holds the stock assets every host may rely on (RIPterm shipped 184 stock `.ICN` icons there - preserved in [`version/1.54/assets/icons/`](../../1.54/assets/icons/README.md)).

requirements.heading: The two directories
requirements.text: A connection directory is optional per connection; when none is configured, the default directory serves both roles. RIPterm could only associate a directory with dialing-directory entries - "if you dial a host by issuing modem commands directly (not using the dialing directory), then the correct directory may not be used since RIPterm has no way of knowing which dialing directory entry you are calling" (RIPTERM.DOC, DIR field notes). A modern implementation should give every connection profile its own directory so the caveat disappears.

If the needed files are not found in that sub-directory, RIPterm will check the ICONS\ sub-directory afterward to see if it is there. This facilitates the concept of \"file overide\" [sic]."

requirements.heading: Resolution order: connection directory first ("file override")
requirements.text: The manual's motivating example is the reason the order matters: sysops independently pick obvious names - "Files like EMAIL.ICN or FILES.ICN would be used on nearly any host! If all these files were located in the same directory, only the very latest installed files would be used when you call a host! In other words, when you call host XYZ, you might see host ABC's EMAIL icon!" (RIPTERM.DOC, same section). Per-connection directories keep same-named assets from different hosts from colliding, and the fallback still lets a host use stock assets by simply not delivering its own copy: "the sysop has the ability to overide [sic] standard icons with his own without affecting the standard icons in any way."

The download directory as set in the General Settings dialog box is not used in this situation as the destination directory." The wire-level delivery flow (RIP_FILE_QUERY → RIP_ENTER_BLOCK_MODE) is the creator-side page [Asset Delivery & Storage](../ripscrip/6.2-asset-delivery-and-storage.md).

requirements.heading: Case-insensitive asset access
requirements.text: **All asset access is case-insensitive.** The original clients ran on DOS (RIPterm) and Windows (RIPtel), whose filesystems are case-insensitive by nature; scripts and hosts freely mix case (`meowbody.ICN`, `CHROME.MSK`), and nothing in the protocol ever compares filenames case-sensitively. An implementation on a case-sensitive filesystem must therefore provide case-insensitive lookup by convention - any equivalent scheme works ([implementation.md - Case Insensitiviy](../../implementation.md#case-insensitiviy)):

requirements.heading: Case-insensitive asset access

- **Lowercase-normalize everything** - store every asset file lowercased and lowercase every requested name before lookup.
- **Self-monitor and index** - pre-load and track the asset directories (watching for changes), resolving requests through a case-folded index that maps to the on-disk names.
- Any other scheme yielding the same observable behavior: a request for `EMAIL.ICN` finds `email.icn`, `Email.Icn`, etc.

requirements.heading: Filename sanitization
requirements.text: Asset filenames on the wire are **bare names**: no drive letters, no path components. The 1.54 spec forbids path information in [RIP_LOAD_ICON](../ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md#rip_load_icon) filenames, and reference implementations enforce it - SyncTERM rejects any name containing `/`, `\`, or `..` before touching the filesystem (`sbbs:src/syncterm/ripper.c` `load_stamp_icon()`; see [Icon Format](3.0-icon-format.md#how-icons-are-referenced-and-stored)). For interfaces requiring bare names, implementation guidance is to reject (do not sanitize-and-accept) path separators, parent-directory references and drive prefixes before filesystem access, rather than accepting a rewritten name. This guidance is not a blanket claim about later clients: RIPtel 3.1’s [FILEDEL macro parser](../../3.0/ripscrip/5.1-text-variables.md#filedel) consumes single backslashes as escapes, rejects forward slashes and retains colons, and its deletion scope includes shared/user search paths. Those exact later-client exceptions are documented separately; do not generalize them to 1.54 loads or received download filenames. Extension defaulting still applies after validation (a name with no `.` gets `.ICN` appended on icon loads).

requirements.heading: RIPscrip 1.54 - Technical Specifications
requirements.text: Original technical documentation for the binary formats and implementation behaviors of the RIPscrip 1.x family (RIPterm 1.52/1.54, RIPaint 1.52), with **1.54** as the definitive release. These pages are **not** part of TeleGrafix's specification text - they document, correct, and extend it from byte-level evidence, and every reverse-engineered claim is cited; anything unverifiable is marked as such.

requirements.heading: RIPscrip 1.54 - Technical Specifications
requirements.text: Language semantics are not repeated here - see the companion [language reference](../ripscrip/README.md); shared terminology is defined in the [glossary](../../glossary.md). Formats are documented in the earliest version where they appear (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#technical-specifications-techspecs)); the [2.0](../../2.0/techspecs/README.md) and [3.0](../../3.0/techspecs/README.md) techspecs document only deltas and link back to these pages.

requirements.heading: Contents
requirements.text:
- **1. Parsing & wire protocol**
  - **[1.0 `.RIP` Stream & File Parsing](1.0-rip-stream-parsing.md)** - byte-level line structure, continuation, escaping, embedded ANSI handling, prologue/epilogue conventions in real files, wild-data hazards (the RIP_LOAD_ICON `res` field)
  - **[1.1 MegaNum Encoding](1.1-meganum-encoding.md)** - digit set, fixed widths per parameter, signedness, implemented edge cases (lowercase, `-` as digit 0, early termination, invalid input)
- **2. Rendering semantics**
  - **[2.0 Canvas, Clipping & Write Modes](2.0-canvas-clipping-write-modes.md)** - viewport clipping behavior, copy/XOR write modes on palette indices, the put-mode family for images, reset semantics
  - **[2.1 Pattern & Fill Rasterization](2.1-pattern-fill-rasterization.md)** - line-pattern anchoring, fill-pattern semantics and alignment, flood-fill behavior, style-0 questions
- **3. File formats**
  - **[3.0 Icon Format (`.ICN` / `.MSK` / `.HIC`)](3.0-icon-format.md)** - byte layout, plane merging, size formula (two trash bytes), mask semantics, worked decode
  - **[3.1 BGI Stroked Fonts (`.CHR`)](3.1-bgi-stroked-fonts.md)** - header, stroke opcodes, metrics, size→scale ratios, RIP font-number mapping
  - **[3.2 Bitmap Fonts (`RIPTERM.FNT`)](3.2-bitmap-fonts.md)** - container layout, charset directory, glyph rasterization and magnification
- **4. Storage & asset delivery**
  - **[4.0 Connection Directory Model](4.0-connection-directory-model.md)** - the storage layout an implementation needs: a per-connection (system) asset directory plus the shared default icons directory; resolution order is connection directory first, then default ("file override" - same-named files from different hosts must not collide); downloads are written to the connection's directory when one is specified, else the default; directory auto-creation on first use; all asset access is case-insensitive, by whatever scheme the client prefers (index, lowercasing, or other); filename sanitization still applies (bare names, no path components - reject traversal)

requirements.heading: 2.x Stream Conventions (delta from 1.54)
requirements.text: The byte-level line grammar of a `.RIP` stream - the `!|` introducer, `|` command delimiter, `\` line continuation and quoting, raw-text pass-through, CR/LF handling - carries over from 1.54 unchanged and is documented in the [1.54 stream & file parsing page](../../1.54/techspecs/1.0-rip-stream-parsing.md); the language-level syntax rules (parameter widths, shortening, escaping) are in the 2.x specification's [Protocol Definition](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md) and are not restated here. What follows is what is **new on the 2.x wire** and what the **shipped 2.x script corpus actually does** - the conventions of the only known authentic RIPscrip 2.x-generation content, which any implementation must play back correctly.

requirements.heading: 2.x Stream Conventions (delta from 1.54)
requirements.text: The corpus: the **36 `.RIP` scripts** in the RIPterm 2.30 distribution's `ICONS\` directory (`~/src/rip-tools/artifacts/ripterm-2.30/extracted/ICONS/*.RIP`, preserved byte-exact in [`version/2.0/assets/icons/`](../../2.0/assets/icons/README.md)), plus the RIPterm Professional 2.0 original of `SHADOW.RIP` (`~/src/rip-tools/RIPTerm2.0/extracted/ICONS/SHADOW.RIP`) - the sole script the 2.0 install shipped, and the only one TeleGrafix later revised, making the pair a unique before/after sample of their own authoring conventions. Every claim below was verified programmatically across all 37 files (byte scans, 2026-08-08); observations that could not be cross-checked against a specification or binary are marked.

requirements.heading: The SOH introducer - `\x01|`
requirements.text: The 2.x specification (rule 12, [Protocol Definition](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md#ripscrip-protocol---syntax-and-general-structure), v2.A3) adds two alternate introducers to the 1.54-only `!`: **Ctrl-A (SOH, byte `0x01`) and Ctrl-B (STX, byte `0x02`)** may replace the exclamation mark, and - unlike `!|` - may start a RIPscrip sequence **mid-line**, after raw text, because BBS hosts strip control characters from user input and so only the host can emit them. The spec's own example is `This is raw text<STX>|c01|@1010hello world`.

requirements.heading: The SOH introducer - `\x01|`
requirements.text: What the shipped corpus does with this license is narrower and very consistent:

requirements.heading: The SOH introducer - `\x01|`
requirements.text:
- **Exactly 18 of the 36 scripts begin with byte `0x01` at file offset 0**, immediately followed by `|` - e.g. `SHADOW.RIP` opens `01 7C 2A 0D 0A` = `\x01|*` + CRLF (SOH, then [RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](../ripscrip/1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows)).
- **SOH never appears anywhere except offset 0.** No file uses it mid-line or on a later line; every subsequent command line uses the classic `!|`.
- **STX (`0x02`) never appears at all** in any shipped 2.x-generation script.
- The 18 files without SOH (the 14 `CYC*` palette-cycle fragments and `EXAMPLE1`-`4`) open with plain `!|`.

requirements.heading: The SOH introducer - `\x01|`
requirements.text: So in practice TeleGrafix used SOH as a **start-of-scene marker on the first line of a standalone scene file** - the reading the RIPscrip 3.0 corpus later makes systematic (111 of 116 RIPtel demo files; see the [3.x protocol notes](../../3.0/ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md)). The revised `SHADOW.RIP` is the clearest evidence that this was a deliberate 2.2-era convention: the 2.0 original opens with the line `!|l7040B040`, and the 2.20/2.30 revision **replaces that line with `\x01|*`** (see [the revision](#the-shadowrip-revision---a-beforeafter-sample) below).

requirements.heading: The SOH introducer - `\x01|`
requirements.text: **What a parser must tolerate:**

requirements.heading: The SOH introducer - `\x01|`
requirements.text:
- Accept `\x01|` and `\x02|` wherever `!|` is accepted - including as the very first bytes of a file - and additionally mid-line after raw text, per the spec rule. A 1.54-only parser that requires `!` will treat the whole first line as raw text and lose the scene's reset.
- Do not require SOH: half the shipped corpus lacks it, and `!|` remains fully valid on line 1.
- After the introducer, parsing is identical to `!|`: commands separated by `|`, terminated by CR/LF or continued with `\`.

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text: Openers across the corpus, by first bytes of the file:

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text: | Opener (observed bytes) | Files | Meaning |

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text: | `\x01\|*` … | DEMOFILE, EAGLE, HAWK, N2_BUSI, N2_PHOTO, N2_TITLE, SHADOW | SOH + reset first |

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text: | `\x01\|1K\|*` … | FOUND, FRACTMTN, RACECAR, SAILBOAT, SHUTTLE, SPACSHUT, TUNNEL | SOH + [RIP_KILL_MOUSE_FIELDS](../ripscrip/4.2-mouse-fields-and-pointer.md#rip_kill_mouse_fields), then reset |

requirements.text: | `\x01\|1K\|w0000000000\|*` … | WEATHER | kill fields, define text window, then reset |

requirements.text: | `\x01\|D…` | FADEIN, FADEOUT | SOH + bulk [RIP_SET_PALETTE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_palette) - **no reset**: palette-fade effects meant to run over an existing scene |

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text: | `\x01\|J10\|n2000\|M08\|fZKQO…` | NEWS | SOH + full setup prologue - **no reset anywhere in the file** |

requirements.text: | `!\|d…` | CYC001DN … CYC111UP (14 files) | no SOH, no reset: palette-cycle animation fragments |

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text: Two prologue idioms recur:

requirements.heading: Prologue conventions
requirements.text:
- **The reset opener** - `|*` (RIP_RESET_WINDOWS), usually preceded by `|1K` so stale mouse fields from the previous scene cannot fire during the redraw. 15 of 36 files contain a reset - 14 exactly one, plus DEMOFILE's playlist, which issues 17 (one before each chained scene); the files without one are deliberately non-destructive (palette fragments, fades, and NEWS, which paints over the full screen).
- **The setup block `!|J10|n2000|M08|fZKQO`** - set Base Math to [MegaNums](../../glossary.md#protocol--syntax) (`J10` - note the shipping engines' level-0 `J` opcode vs the ALPHA 4 draft's colliding `b`; see the [RIP_SET_BASE_MATH editor's note](../ripscrip/1.2-math-and-coordinates.md#rip_set_base_math)), 2-digit coordinates ([RIP_SET_COORDINATE_SIZE](../ripscrip/1.2-math-and-coordinates.md#rip_set_coordinate_size)), color-mapping mode with 8-bit palette ([RIP_SET_COLOR_MODE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_color_mode)), and a 1280×960 world frame ([RIP_SET_WORLD_FRAME](../ripscrip/1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_set_world_frame), `ZK`=1280, `QO`=960). EXAMPLE1-4 and NEWS open with it; thirteen more files carry the identical block in their branding footer (below). It restates the post-reset defaults - the corpus treats explicit state setup as cheap insurance, and the exact same block opens 90 of 116 RIPtel scripts ([3.x notes](../../3.0/ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md)).
- **Client-chrome queries** - DEMOFILE and the three `N2_*` files follow the reset with `|1\x1b0000$SBAROFF$`: [RIP_QUERY](../ripscrip/5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_query) (level 1, command character = the literal **ESC byte `0x1B`**) carrying the `$SBAROFF$` text variable to hide the client's status bar before the scene draws.

requirements.heading: Epilogue conventions
requirements.text:
- **`!|#|#|#`** - a triple [RIP_NO_MORE](../ripscrip/1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md#rip_no_more) is the standard scene terminator: **20 of 36 files end with exactly the line `!|#|#|#`** (CRLF-terminated). NEWS.RIP ends with it twice on consecutive lines. The files without it are the 14 `CYC*` fragments and FADEIN/FADEOUT - the non-scene animation/palette fragments, which contain no `#` at all.
- **The demo-branding footer** - 14 files close with a shared block (EAGLE, EXAMPLE1-4, FOUND, FRACTMTN, HAWK, NEWS, SAILBOAT, SHADOW, SHUTTLE, SPACSHUT, TUNNEL): the `!|J10|n2000|M08|fZKQO` setup restated, an Atech font selection ([RIP_EXTENDED_FONT_STYLE](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_extended_font_style) `|y…Dixon`), a [RIP_BUTTON_STYLE](../ripscrip/4.3-buttons.md#rip_button_style) + [RIP_BUTTON](../ripscrip/4.3-buttons.md#rip_button) pair whose button carries an empty `<><>` icon/label/host-command triple (a decorative beveled plaque), and two [RIP_TEXT_XY](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_text_xy) lines - a copyright line (usually "Copyright ¿ 1995 TeleGrafix Communications, Inc.", the `¿` is byte `0xA8` read as CP437 and the Dixon outline font evidently maps it to a © glyph) and "For Demonstration Purposes Only" - then `!|#|#|#`. Example, the FRACTMTN.RIP tail:

requirements.heading: Epilogue conventions
requirements.text:
```text
!|J10|n2000|M08|fZKQO|y00000W0M000000001a1a000000Dixon
!|1B0000020PVK040F000F080700000F07000000|1U05ODCDQI0000<><>|c00|W03
!|y00000W0L000000001a1a000000Dixon
!|@5YP5Copyright ¿ 1995 TeleGrafix Communications, Inc.
!|@68Q0For Demonstration Purposes Only|#|#|#
```

requirements.heading: Epilogue conventions
requirements.text: Three more files carry part of it: WEATHER.RIP has the font and both branding text lines but no button; N2_BUSI.RIP has the font and a copyright line with variant wording ("For Demonstration Purpose Only!"); N2_TITLE.RIP and N2_PHOTO.RIP close with a bare `!|J10|n2000|M08|fZKQO|#|#|#`. Eighteen files carry the setup block somewhere.

requirements.heading: Epilogue conventions
requirements.text: - **Trailing line ending** - every file's last line is CRLF-terminated; FADEOUT.RIP and the 2.0-era SHADOW.RIP additionally end with one blank line (a bare final CRLF). No file ends mid-line.

requirements.heading: Line structure, endings and lengths
requirements.text:
- **CRLF exclusively.** All 37 surveyed files use `\r\n` on every line - zero lone `\n`, zero lone `\r` (significant: the RIPtel corpus does contain bare-CR files, but no 2.x-generation one does).
- **Command lines keep an 80-column discipline: the longest line beginning `!|` or `\x01|` in the corpus is 78 bytes** (EAGLE.RIP polygon lines, including their trailing `\`). Continuation payload lines reach 77 bytes.
- **Raw text lines do not honor that limit: NEWS.RIP contains a 104-byte flowed-text line** ("Pirating the software is the same as robbing us of the dream. Would you want someone to ruin your dr…"). A parser must not clamp or split lines at 80 bytes.
- **`\` continuation is heavy production traffic, not an edge case.** 7 files use it; FADEIN.RIP is 1,024 physical lines of which **960 are continuations** - 64 RIP_SET_PALETTE commands, each spanning ~16 physical lines (~1,070 argument characters). Continuation lines carry **no introducer** - they are bare argument bytes (e.g. EAGLE.RIP line 2 ends `…4D79\`, line 3 opens `4U6L52…`), so a parser mid-command must consume the next physical line as argument data, not restart line classification.
- **Command density** - multi-command lines are the norm: up to 13 `|`-separated commands per line (`FRACTMTN.RIP`, e.g. line 42: twelve RIP_PIXEL plus a RIP_COLOR), and DEMOFILE's playlist puts a scene load plus two delays on one line: `!|*|1R00000000TUNNEL.RIP|3D008C|3D0060`.

requirements.heading: Raw text and modal text flow
requirements.text: Rule 6 of the protocol (a line not beginning with an introducer is raw text for the [text window](../../glossary.md#display-model)) carries over from 1.54 - but the corpus shows a **second, modal meaning** of raw lines: NEWS.RIP defines four linked text-column regions with [RIP_BEGIN_TEXT](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_begin_text) (`|1T…01/11/21/31`) and then flows its multi-paragraph newspaper article as **dozens of raw text lines with no introducer at all**, which the client pours into the graphics-side columns - not the TTY text window. Blank raw lines separate paragraphs. Notably, NEWS.RIP never sends the spec's [RIP_END_TEXT](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_end_text) (`|1E`) or the spec's per-line [RIP_REGION_TEXT](../ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_region_text) wrapper: the flow simply ends when the next `!|` command line arrives. The full column/stream mechanism was only formalized in 3.0 - the reconstruction, which uses this same NEWS.RIP as evidence, is in the [3.x column-text-system page](../../3.0/ripscrip/3.1-column-text-system.md); a 2.x implementation needs at minimum the modal rule: after a `1T` region definition, raw lines are flowed article text until a command line ends the block.

requirements.heading: Multi-level command parsing notes
requirements.text: Observed level usage across all shipped 2.x-generation scripts:

requirements.heading: Multi-level command parsing notes
requirements.text:
- **Levels 0, 1 and 3 only.** No shipped script uses level 2, level 9, or any multi-digit sub-level (`|15L`-style, spec rule 8) - those paths ship untested by original content.
- **Level 3 interleaves freely with level 0** as animation pacing: each `CYC*` file is 64 repetitions of `!|d<entry><bits><rgb>|3D0001` - one [RIP_ONE_DRAWING_PALETTE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_one_drawing_palette) step (UltraNum RGB argument regardless of Base Math) followed by a one-tick [RIP_DELAY](../ripscrip/5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_delay). DEMOFILE chains whole scenes with `|1R` ([RIP_READ_SCENE](../ripscrip/5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_read_scene)) plus `|3D` delays.
- **The command-type character can be a control byte.** Five files (DEMOFILE, N2_BUSI, N2_PHOTO, N2_TITLE, TUNNEL) use `|1\x1b` - RIP_QUERY's command character is the literal ESC byte `0x1B`, the only non-printing command character in the corpus. Tokenizers that assume printable command characters will mis-parse these files.
- **Level parsing rule** (unchanged from the spec): after `|`, consume decimal digits `1`-`9` as the level/sub-level string (a leading `0` is not a level digit), then exactly one command-type character, which may be any character from the spec's set - plus, per the corpus, ESC.

requirements.heading: Repeated state-sets - the `|k00` pattern
requirements.text: `|k` is [RIP_BACK_COLOR](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_back_color). The 2.0-era SHADOW.RIP emits `|k00` (background = color 0) **160 times** - once on nearly every one of its 170 text-drawing lines, alongside 5 `|k0A` and 5 `|k0C`; the 2.30 revision keeps the drawing identical but strips the redundant repeats down to 10 `|k00` (the `|k0A`/`|k0C` uses survive unchanged). Elsewhere the corpus still carries scattered redundant state-sets (`|k00` once in each `N2_*` file, twice in WEATHER). Implication for implementers: authored 2.x-generation streams re-assert unchanged state constantly; state commands must be cheap and idempotent, and stream-diffing tools should expect this noise.

requirements.heading: The SHADOW.RIP revision - a before/after sample
requirements.text: The discarded opener `!|l7040B040` deserves a parser note: in the ALPHA 4 specification, level-0 `l` is [RIP_POLYLINE](../ripscrip/2.1-lines.md#rip_polyline), but the arguments do not parse as one (`70` would declare 252 points with only 8 argument characters following). Whether it is a pre-release 2.0 command or simply malformed is **not established** - what matters is that the shipping 2.0 client visibly played the file anyway, i.e. it discarded the unparseable command per the spec's corruption rule (rule 15: a hopelessly corrupted command is dropped and the parser resynchronizes at the next `|` delimiter - here, end of line). An implementation should do the same: skip, don't abort.

requirements.heading: What carries over from 1.54 unchanged
requirements.text: Everything not listed above - verified present and unchanged across the corpus:

requirements.heading: What carries over from 1.54 unchanged
requirements.text:
- The `!|` introducer at column 0, `|` as universal command delimiter, and multiple commands per line ([1.54 stream parsing](../../1.54/techspecs/1.0-rip-stream-parsing.md)).
- `\`-before-CRLF line continuation and `\`-quoting of literal `!`, `|`, `\` in text parameters (spec rules 5, 11, 13 - the quoting corner cases carry v1.54 tags in the 2.x spec).
- Raw-text pass-through to the text window for lines without an introducer (modal column-flow excepted, above).
- MegaNum base-36 parameters as the default numbering ([1.1 MegaNum encoding](../../1.54/techspecs/1.1-meganum-encoding.md)); the 2.x additions - Base Math switching and UltraNum parameters - are language-level and covered by the [glossary](../../glossary.md#protocol--syntax) and the 2.x spec pages.
- CRLF line termination as authored; the corpus contains no counterexample requiring bare-LF or bare-CR tolerance, though accepting them costs nothing and the 3.x corpus does require bare-CR handling.

requirements.heading: What carries over from 1.54 unchanged
requirements.text: [Contents](README.md) · [Next: Canvas Tiers, Palette & RGB ▶](2.0-canvas-palette-rgb.md)

requirements.heading: Canvas Tiers, Palette & RGB Rendering
requirements.text: RIPscrip 2.x breaks the 1.54 ceiling of 16 colors from a 64-color master palette: a 256-entry drawing palette plus an optional direct-RGB color mode with arbitrary bit precision. What the spec leaves open: the logical canvas/resolution tiers and color depths the shipping client actually rendered to, and how palette and RGB values resolve to pixels on them.

requirements.heading: Canvas Tiers, Palette & RGB Rendering
requirements.text: _The language side is fully specified in [Color, Audio & Text Windows](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md) and is not restated here._

requirements.heading: Language surface (spec links)
requirements.text:
- **Drawing palette** - the 256-entry color lookup table ([The Drawing Palette](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#the-drawing-palette)); entries 0-15 remain the legacy 16-color "desktop palette" still adjustable by the 1.54 [RIP_SET_PALETTE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_palette)/[RIP_ONE_PALETTE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_one_palette); the full table is addressed by [RIP_ONE_DRAWING_PALETTE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_one_drawing_palette) and [RIP_SET_DRAWING_PALETTE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_drawing_palette), whose RGB parameters are four-digit base-64 [UltraNums](../../glossary.md#protocol--syntax) regardless of the base-math setting.
- **Direct-RGB mode** - [RIP_SET_COLOR_MODE](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_color_mode) and the [`$COLORMODE$`](../ripscrip/5.1-text-variables.md#colormode) environment variable; resolution semantics in [Palette Mapping and Direct RGB Mode](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#palette-mapping-and-direct-rgb-mode), component bit-scaling rules included.
- **Default palette** - on any reset the 256 entries load the fixed table (16 ANSI colors, 16-step gray ramp, 224-entry RGB cube indexed `INDEX = 32 + BLUE + GREEN*4 + RED*32`) transcribed in full in [Default RGB Values of Color Lookup Table](../ripscrip/2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#default-rgb-values-of-color-lookup-table).

requirements.heading: Language surface (spec links)
requirements.text: One shipped-client corroboration worth recording: the same 16-color, gray-ramp, and RGB-cube DAC blocks appear **verbatim** (6-bit VGA DAC triplets) inside the client's resource container - observed in the RIPtel-era client resource file ([research notes](../../3.0/research/riptel-resource-containers.md#ripscripres---client-resource-container)) - so the shipping engine's default palette is byte-for-byte the specified table, not an approximation.

requirements.heading: Resolution tiers as shipped
requirements.text: RIPscrip itself never selects a video mode - the client owns the display, and the world-coordinate system ([RIP_SET_WORLD_FRAME](../ripscrip/1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_set_world_frame)) exists precisely so scenes are resolution-independent. What matters to an implementation is the set of logical canvases the definitive client rendered to:
