requirements.heading: Text-window Geometry Query Grammar
requirements.text: **Normative reconciliation:** The inherited ALPHA 4 query descriptions conflict: TWX1's syntax block advertises COLS/default COLS, while its prose and TWY1 specify WORLD/DEVICE for explicit graphical queries; TWW/TWH's early DOMAIN restriction contradicts their later TEXT-domain descriptions. The following common contract resolves those conflicts for this 3.0 reference. The coordinate-query prose governs explicit TYPE, and the dimension queries retain their expressly described TEXT domains. This is an editorial reconciliation of intended protocol rules, **not** a claim that the original RIPtel 3.1 argument decoder implements every accepted call. Its shared defaults and malformed/inverted acceptance paths are source limits, not additional protocol requirements. [Derivation and exact source boundaries](../research/issue-108-text-window-query-grammar.md).
requirements.note: Reconciled against adopted PR #111/#114/#115 with independent native and connected expected results. Button rendering, hover and synchronous playback remain separate pending clauses.

requirements.heading: Text-window Geometry Query Grammar
requirements.text: TWX0, TWX1, TWY0, TWY1, TWW and TWH take `WINDOW,TYPE,DOMAIN` in that order, with only trailing arguments optional. WINDOW defaults to the current TW and accepts `CUR` or a decimal window number `0..35`. Supply WINDOW (using CUR if desired) before TYPE, and TYPE before DOMAIN; empty arguments do not skip positions. Keywords are ASCII case-insensitive. The normal [dollar-call byte and argument rules](#argument-bytes-and-local-backslashes) still apply. Results are decimal integers, independent of Base Math.

requirements.heading: Text-window Geometry Query Grammar
requirements.text: This table is exhaustive. CELL is not a position-query TYPE. COLS and ROWS are never position-query domains; there is no explicit cell-corner domain. A mismatched count domain (TWW,ROWS or TWH,COLS), a count domain with BOUND/CELL, an unknown keyword or an extra argument is a syntax error, not a geometry result. For example, `$TWX1(CUR,TEXT,COLS)$`, `$TWY1(CUR,TEXT,ROWS)$`, `$TWW(CUR,TEXT,ROWS)$` and `$TWH(CUR,CELL,ROWS)$` are invalid. In contrast, `$TWX1(CUR,TEXT)$` is a WORLD edge, while `$TWW(CUR,TEXT)$` is a column count.
requirements.note: Reconciled against adopted PR #111/#114/#115 with independent native and connected expected results. Button rendering, hover and synchronous playback remain separate pending clauses.

requirements.heading: Text-window Geometry Query Grammar
requirements.text: For any valid form, an **undefined or inactive** target returns `-1` for any of the four position queries, or `0` for TWW/TWH. For a defined, active **extended** window, only the omitted-TYPE position form returns `-1`; its graphical position forms and all accepted dimension forms work normally. These are metadata queries: they do not create/select/activate a window, move a live or saved cursor, change protection, modes, margins, terminal parsing or any graphics family, paint pixels or execute a resident query. A noncurrent target remains noncurrent. No VT-102 implementation is required by this query contract.
requirements.note: Reconciled against adopted PR #111/#114/#115 with independent native and connected expected results. Button rendering, hover and synchronous playback remain separate pending clauses.

requirements.heading: Edges, counts and conversion
requirements.text: For an ordinary [`w`](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_text_window) definition, omitted-TYPE positions are its stored cell corners: near X/Y, and near X/Y plus columns/rows **minus one** for far X/Y. They use absolute ordinary cell coordinates, not coordinates relative to the window's live cursor. Thus the far cell is inclusive, matching `w` input; this form is not obtained by dividing a graphical edge by the loaded font's dimensions. Extended [`b`](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_extended_text_window) definitions have no such ordinary cell-origin coordinates, even if they happen to align with the font grid.
requirements.note: Reconciled against adopted PR #111/#114/#115 with independent native and connected expected results. Button rendering, hover and synchronous playback remain separate pending clauses.

requirements.heading: Edges, counts and conversion
requirements.text: For explicit TEXT/BOUND, X0/Y0 return the stored near edges and X1/Y1 the stored **exclusive** far edges of the chosen display/bounding rectangle. A last included device pixel at X=299 therefore gives X1=300. A dimension is right−left or bottom−top in device coordinates. Ordinary windows have coincident bounding and display rectangles; extended windows may have a smaller, centered display inside the bound. CELL uses the selected font's actual device metrics, including successfully loaded MAF metrics; it is not a nominal-grid replacement for those metrics. See [extended fitting](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#fitting-the-text-window).
requirements.note: Reconciled against adopted PR #111/#114/#115 with independent native and connected expected results. Button rendering, hover and synchronous playback remain separate pending clauses.

requirements.heading: Edges, counts and conversion
requirements.text: DEVICE returns that device edge or length directly. WORLD converts the device value using the **current environment's** WORLD and physical device extents on the corresponding axis: `deviceValue * worldExtent / deviceExtent`, with integer division toward zero (floor for nonnegative values). Convert a queried length once after device-edge subtraction; do not subtract two separately rounded WORLD edge results. A definition's earlier WORLD setting is not a permanently stored query domain. Cell counts and legacy cell corners undergo no WORLD conversion.

requirements.reason: Connected current/default TW supports CON/COFF and zero-based TWGOTO/TWHOME through native owner services. Selectors and optional axes are fully prevalidated; no/only-WINNO TWGOTO has no effect. Coordinates are decimal regardless of ENV radix; legal 20-digit values saturate safely and clamp to actual full window bounds before narrowing. CUR retains the chosen owner target axis. Undefined slots and deactivated windows ignore cursor operations. Visibility changes retain native shape/mode and pending wrap, survive later text and reset cached mode on ANSI reset. ATW restores its saved renderer gate before same-expansion CON/COFF effects. Incoming malformed references and callback failures recover inside the parser without ending the session. Independent host callbacks exercise noncurrent targets; connected acceptance covers default/current entry and positioned windows in CP437/UTF-8 on three reference rasters. Complete TW table/selection/protection and persistent defined noncurrent views remain pending; metadata/basic predicates do not claim those lifecycles.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: This command moves the cursor in the specified text window data table entry to the upper-left corner of the window. WINNO may be any value from 0-35 to indicate the desired data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the WINNO slot number happens to correspond to the current text window or the WINNO parameter is specified as "CUR" then the cursor that is on the screen (potentially) will be visibly moved. If the WINNO parameter specifies a window that is not the current text window then the cursor position definition for that non-current window is altered only - no visible thing would happen on the screen.
requirements.reason: Connected 36-slot owner retains native window state and routes current/noncurrent effects independently of current selection. requirements.heading: $AVP$
requirements.text: This command does the exact opposite of the [`$DVP$`](#dvp) text variable which deactivates a viewport. When a viewport is activated, it no longer discards graphical commands that are sent to it. This does not make any visual changes on the screen immediately - they only affect subsequent graphical RIPscrip operations that are received when that viewport is selected as the current viewport. You may activate more then one viewport by specifying multiple viewport slot numbers.

requirements.heading: $EGW$

Screen erasures affect shared pixels plus any overlapping text. Bitmap erasures affect each selected bitmap's own storage. requirements.heading: $MVP$
requirements.text: For each eligible port, set its stored viewport to the full RIP screen canvas in DEVICE coordinates, `[0,0,screen_width,screen_height)`. Copy those half-open bounds directly for both screen and bitmap ports. The operation changes only the stored viewport. Port bounds, bitmap allocation, pixels, selection and other fields are retained. Drawing and queries use the stored rectangle under their usual conversion rules. Raster access remains limited to the target backing surface. HEADER 2048/4096 uses the same geometry. [Viewport coordinates](1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_viewport) · [HEADER geometry](1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md#port-bounds-reset-and-black-fill) · [Rectangle derivation](../research/issue-301-viewport-maximize-rectangle.md).

requirements.heading: Port query grammar and RIPtel 3.1 status
requirements.text: Thus the parser accepts `$PORTW$`, `$PORTW(CUR)$`, `$PORTW(CUR,PORT)$`, `$PORTW(CUR,VIEW)$` and `$PORTW(CUR,VIEW,DEVICE)$`; substitute any of the other five names without changing the grammar. A numeric selector remains decimal regardless of Base Math; leading zeroes are accepted. **`(portno,DEVICE)` and `(portno,WORLD)` are not shorthands**: the second field is always a type. Specify `(portno,PORT,DEVICE)` or `(portno,VIEW,DEVICE)` instead. PORTY1 has no separate `(viewno,coordtype)` form. Blank comma fields are discarded by the ordinary variable parser rather than reserving missing positions, so `(CUR,,DEVICE)` cannot skip the type.
requirements.reason: Live RIP_QUERY tests check all six variables with positional defaults, discarded empty comma fields, mixed-case keywords, decimal selectors with leading zeroes in Base Math 64, and invalid grammar followed by a valid reference. The native test covers the complete selector, type and domain combinations.

requirements.heading: Port query grammar and RIPtel 3.1 status
requirements.text: **Shipped callback defect:** the decoder returns success for these valid forms, but all six RIPtel 3.1 callbacks invert that result, set the variable-error flag and return no value. Ordinary macro expansion leaves each complete expression unchanged; it does not produce the intended numeric width/height/coordinate or sentinel. Invalid forms can fall into calculation with partially uninitialized decoded state, so do not treat an accidental result as an alternate supported grammar or assume a clean rejection. The per-variable dimension descriptions/examples below describe the intended query, not a successful original-client reply. This extends the earlier confirmed PORTW/PORTH defect to the four corner queries; no numerical calculation has been patched to make it pass.

requirements.heading: $APP$
requirements.text: This text variable instructs the terminal to execute an external application. If you do not specify any parameters, then application number zero will be executed. If you do specify any parameters, you may specify one or both of them. If you supply the ARGUMENT parameter, you must specify the APPNO option. APPNO is a number from 0-9 indicating which application should be executed. If used, the ARGUMENT parameter is an arbitrary command line argument that will be added to the end of the application's command line string. This gives the ability to allow the host to control portions of the external application's operation.

requirements.reason: Introductory description or table heading.

requirements.heading: $BAUDEMUL$
requirements.text: **RIPtel 3.1 format:** `$BAUDEMUL$` or `$BAUDEMUL(rate)$`

requirements.heading: $BAUDEMUL$
requirements.text: With zero parsed arguments, substitute the current interpreter's live rate in decimal. `$BAUDEMUL()$` is also a query. A value of `0` means full speed. With exactly one nonempty decimal argument, set that live rate and substitute an empty string. For portable input, use ASCII digits and a value in 0–2,147,483,647. Reject values outside that range.

requirements.heading: $BAUDEMUL$
requirements.text: `$BAUDEMUL(2400)$` sets 2,400. A subsequent `$BAUDEMUL$` substitutes `2400` even if the active ENV has changed. A lone numeric argument such as `$BAUDEMUL(35)$` is a request to set 35. The inherited draft's ENV-qualified forms are different. `$BAUDEMUL(CUR)$` and `$BAUDEMUL(5,2400)$` fail the original digit/count checks and do not change the rate. The same applies to other nondecimal input or extra parsed arguments. The enclosing expander follows the [rejected built-in rule](5.2-templates-and-conditionals.md#eligible-providers-and-rejected-codes).

requirements.heading: $BAUDEMUL$
requirements.text: The getter and setter use the same [live value as the wire command](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#live-playback-rate-and-env-state). ENV selection and ordinary SOFT reset preserve the rate. `SENV` and `RENV` capture and restore it as a separate value alongside the ENV table and index. [RIPtel 3.1 derivation](../research/issue-172-local-playback-baud.md)

requirements.heading: $BSMODE$
requirements.text: _Query or set ANSI text backspace erasure_
requirements.reason: Capability heading.

requirements.heading: $BSMODE$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$BSMODE$`, `$BSMODE(QUERY)$`, `$BSMODE(DEST)$`, `$BSMODE(NONDEST)$`.

requirements.heading: $BSMODE$
requirements.text: With zero parsed arguments or the single keyword `QUERY`, substitute ASCII `1` for destructive mode or `0` for nondestructive mode. `DEST` enables erasure and `NONDEST` disables it. Successful setters substitute an empty string. See the [ANSI receive and echo rules](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#ansi-backspace-and-key-transmission) for the affected cells and the setting's lifetime.
requirements.scope: The explicit BSMODE command's grammar, query reply and update of the supported erasure setting. Default ANSI Backspace and local echo remain terminal policy.

requirements.heading: $BSXMIT$
requirements.text: _Query or set the byte sent for an ordinary Backspace keystroke_
requirements.reason: Capability heading.

requirements.heading: $BSXMIT$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$BSXMIT$`, `$BSXMIT(QUERY)$`, `$BSXMIT(DEL)$`, `$BSXMIT(BS)$`.

requirements.heading: $BSXMIT$
requirements.text: With zero parsed arguments or the single keyword `QUERY`, RIPtel 3.1 substitutes ASCII `0` for DEL mode or `1` for BS mode. `DEL` selects byte `7f` and `BS` selects byte `08` for ordinary unmodified Backspace. Successful setters substitute an empty string. When the key generates the ordinary Backspace event, Ctrl reverses the transmitted byte in DEL mode and in half-duplex BS mode. The [key and wire rules](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#ansi-backspace-and-key-transmission) cover local echo and generated output separately.
requirements.scope: The explicit BSXMIT command's grammar, query reply and BS/DEL selection through the terminal interface. Ctrl+Backspace and half-duplex behavior are client key handling.

requirements.heading: $BSXMIT$
requirements.text: Both providers accept case-insensitive keywords. Empty parentheses give zero parsed arguments. An unrecognized keyword or excess parsed arguments rejects the reference without updating the setting. Both are [mixed data/active providers](5.2-templates-and-conditionals.md#eligible-providers-and-rejected-codes), so a successful setter also takes effect in an eligible graphical consumer. [Original RIPtel 3.1 derivation](../research/issue-209-backspace-modes.md)

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: _Delay for a number of sixtieths of a second_

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1; revised in v2.A2._
requirements.reason: Syntax label, historical introduction or corpus provenance; executable D rules and unresolved units/continuation are tracked on neighboring rows.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$D(duration)$`
requirements.reason: A host delay pauses and resumes the response.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: **Syntax:** `$D(required:duration)$`; documented ordinary range **1..65535**, in **60ths of a second**, not milliseconds.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: RIPtel 3.1 converts the duration to an integer-millisecond clock interval, truncating the fraction: **`floor(duration × 1000 / 60)`** for ordinary values. Its original helper divides long waits into 3900-tick (65000 ms) chunks plus the final floored remainder; these chunks preserve the same total conversion.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: | Expression  | Converted clock interval           |

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: | `$D(1)$`    | **16 ms**, from truncating 1000/60 |

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: These are timer targets, not exact wall-clock durations; clock granularity, phase and scheduling affect elapsed time. The summary's inherited "milliseconds" wording was incorrect. The detailed tick rule and [inventory](9.1-text-variable-reference.md#terminal-operation) units were correct.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: The variable performs a **synchronous busy wait** on the evaluating thread, polling `timeGetTime` until each deadline. The variable callback and the separate wire command call the same timer helper. Ordinary macro expansion continues on the same call stack after the wait and emits no replacement text. [Wire RIP_DELAY](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_delay).
requirements.reason: Describes the original synchronous implementation and its shared timer, while the portable duration and continuation behavior are covered by adjacent requirements.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: **Shipped validation quirks:** exactly one argument is required, but the original callback checks only that its first character is a digit before decimal prefix conversion. It has no explicit 1..65535 gate: `$D(0)$` and `$D(65536)$` are accepted; `$D(1A)$` and `$D(1.5)$` behave as `$D(1)$`. A leading sign, space, letter or empty value rejects the variable. These observations do not extend the documented portable range to arbitrary oversized numeric conversions. The helper also compares unsigned absolute timer deadlines without rollover correction; a deadline that wraps can finish early. _Evidence: original registered callback/helper and exhaustive 0..65536/boundary/prefix/fake-clock tests; [derivation](../research/issue-46-delay-variable-units.md)._

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$D(60)$` targets a one-second pause. **Returns:** nothing on success.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: `$D(1)$` is the single most-used variable in the demo corpus (197 uses, pacing the wipe effects). _Evidence: original RIPtel 3.1 driver; 2.00a4; HLP (`tvarProcD`); corpus (SHADOW.FN, WIPE\*.FN); [derivation](../research/issue-46-delay-variable-units.md)._

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**
requirements.reason: Reference history, provenance or table heading.

```text

             ────────
```

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: Deletes the **first existing match for each supplied filename**, using ordinary resource resolution: **configured host directory → shared ICONS directory → user icon-search-path entries in order**. Without a configured host directory, start with shared ICONS, then the search path. Only that first match is passed to deletion; a failed deletion does not fall through to another directory. A missing filename is ignored. Case and the supplied extension are retained; no default extension or legacy ICN/HIC/MSK renaming is performed here.
requirements.reason: SyncTERM permits deletion of regular files only in the active directory of the connected BBS's RIP cache. The Global RIP Directory remains read-only. Lookup uses the supplied extension and ignores absent files.
requirements.scope: Process named deletions through the per-BBS cache, including earlier downloads in that cache. Shared RIP assets are read-only.

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: At least one parsed argument is required. Each argument is processed independently, and failure for one does not stop later arguments. This active variable returns no text and supplies no per-file success result; failed lookups/deletions do not set a variable error. Zero arguments set the variable syntax-error flag. Generic parsing limits each argument to 20 characters and omits empty comma fields; `FILEDEL()` therefore has no arguments.
requirements.reason: The handler requires at least one parsed filename and attempts each independently without a reply or a session error.

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: **The host-created restriction is a caller precondition.** The inherited specification requires the host to name only files it created or downloaded. RIPtel 3.1's original deletion path has **no ownership ledger, creator/session check or host identity check**: a preexisting shared/search-path file can be its first match. Changing connections or sessions does not create such a check. User search paths are consequently eligible for FILEDEL deletion even though asset delivery does not write new files there.
requirements.reason: The writable per-BBS cache defines FILEDEL authority. Historical shared-directory deletion and creator tracking are outside the agreed storage model.

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: **Path syntax in the original macro expression:** hosts should supply bare filenames. The inherited “path information will be ignored” statement is not a uniform basename rule. The ordinary dollar-argument parser rejects `/`, wildcards and several punctuation characters; a single backslash acts as an escape and disappears before lookup. The examples below are literal macro-expression characters supplied to the expander, after any surrounding transport/command decoding:
requirements.reason: The ordinary argument decoder handles local escapes and preserves spaces. Malformed filename lists remain literal through host expansion. Connected tests check the reply and actual files in the selected BBS cache.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: _Test whether a local resource name resolves_
requirements.reason: Introductory, test setup or provenance text for the FILEEXISTS contract.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$FILEEXISTS(filename)$`

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: **Returns:** ASCII `1` for a local match or ASCII `0` for a valid lookup that misses.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: This data variable is eligible in both ordinary HCL and the graphical data pass. It replaces the reference with one byte and continues the enclosing text. Any transmission comes from that consumer, such as a completed HCL response.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text:
1. Require exactly one parsed argument under the [ordinary argument grammar](#argument-bytes-and-local-backslashes). The 20-byte decoded bound and empty-field handling apply. For example, `FILEEXISTS()` has zero arguments and `FILEEXISTS(A,B)` has two. An argument is literal data after decoding. It receives no further variable expansion, wildcard interpretation or playback name substitutions.
2. Apply the [ASCII filename-tail predicate](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#name-preparation-and-lookup). Reject an empty name or unacceptable final byte. Otherwise take the longest acceptable trailing run. Split that result into DOS path components, retain only name and extension, and uppercase ASCII a..z. A drive prefix supplies no search root. Lookup adds no default extension.
3. Run these rewrites **in order** on the current working name: `.ICN→.BMP`, `.HIC→.BMH`, `.MSK→.BMM`. Each rule finds the first occurrence of its old marker and replaces that marker and the remaining suffix with the new marker. Continue with the next rule even after a match. For example, `A.MSK.ICN` becomes `A.MSK.BMP` and then `A.BMM`.
4. Search the configured host directory, shared `ICONS` and the configured icon search path in order. Start at `ICONS` when there is no host directory. Return on the first match. The callback checks existence without opening the resource or requesting retrieval.
requirements.reason: Use the active BBS RIP cache and the read-only Global RIP Directory as authorized by the user. Lookup opens no files.
requirements.scope: Check literal filename existence through the supported RIP resolution policy. Use the per-BBS RIP cache and the shared read-only RIP directory; the cache owns all host-writable paths.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: A wrong argument count or unusable filename tail is a built-in rejection. The original checks report a local argument diagnostic. The surrounding expansion retains the rejected reference and provides neither `0` nor a same-name user-variable fallback. A syntactically invalid argument can be rejected by the dollar parser before the callback. For example, `$FILEEXISTS(A/B)$` does not reach name preparation.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: [`RIP_FILE_QUERY`](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_file_query) sends its own mode-specific record and may open the file for metadata. It stops after the first matching legacy-marker rule. `FILEEXISTS` instead supplies data to surrounding text and applies all three alias rules in order. It has no mode, reserved digits, metadata fields or intrinsic line ending.

requirements.heading: $FILEEXISTS$
requirements.text: For these examples, the connection's resource directories contain `README.RIP` and `EDGE.BMM`, with no `README`, `MISSING.RIP` or `EDGE.MSK`. In an ordinary response, surround the reference with `R=` and `.DONE`. In graphical text, use those same surrounding bytes in a `T` argument. The response sends the substituted bytes and `T` draws those bytes.

requirements.heading: Status-bar state and presentation
requirements.text: The status bar is a terminal presentation option shared across the session's drawing ports and text windows. The setting starts enabled. A set takes effect when the action is evaluated, including for subsequent queries in the same host expression. Repeating the same set leaves the setting at the requested value.
requirements.reason: Connected status setting, display composition and underlying canvas behavior under PR #202.

requirements.heading: Status-bar state and presentation
requirements.text: **Portable profile.** Use the client's existing status indicator when one is available. Show or hide it according to the setting. A client without a usable indicator implements the same logical switch and query results without drawing a row. Either implementation advertises `STATBAR` in [OPTION(LIST)](#option), whether the setting is on or off. The query reports the setting even when the indicator is temporarily obscured or the client has nowhere to draw it. A client-local control for this same indicator updates the same setting.
requirements.reason: Connected status setting, display composition and underlying canvas behavior under PR #202.

requirements.heading: Status-bar state and presentation
requirements.text:
- Preserve the RIP device extent and WORLD mapping. `RESX`/`RESY`, PORT0's bounds and viewport, and other RIP port definitions keep their values. A status row takes no rows out of the RIP address space.
- Preserve the current ANSI text-window selection, activation, bounds, cell grid, contents and cursor state. Do not shrink the window, reserve an ANSI row, clear cells, scroll text or reflow it when the setting changes.
- Present the indicator in separate terminal chrome or composite it over the completed canvas. Keep the indicator out of PORT0's backing pixels. A shared surface may temporarily cover content, and hiding the indicator reveals the current underlying pixels, including any drawing received while it was shown. The toggle itself performs no RIP drawing.
- [SCREEN backups](7.2-data-backup-areas.md#screen-save-area) capture the underlying canvas and current palette RGB. The setting and indicator graphics stay outside SCREEN and the aggregate SAVEALL/RESTOREALL operations.
requirements.reason: Connected status setting, display composition and underlying canvas behavior under PR #202.

requirements.heading: $SHIFT$

requirements.reason: Parser-owned local data dispatch implements SHIFT/CTRL through a nonblocking borrowed modifier provider, MSTAT from explicit installed-mouse state and COLORS from independent device capacity. XY uses captured DEVICE coordinates, current ENV before fallback frame, signed truncating WORLD conversion, explicit low-WORD narrowing and minimum-width decimal formatting; text-query omission instead computes/clamps an explicit resolved device cell grid. All missing services remain unsupported, without physical probing or input injection. Independent native all-canvas published XY/cell replies, negative/boundary/WORD cases, current/protected ENV precedence, live local-state changes, literal capacity cases and nonfatal malformed/missing/provider-failure recovery pass. A delayed compound query demonstrates read-when-reached and queued-source ordering, and real local data callbacks feed the existing non-short-circuit condition evaluator. Platform adapters and full angle/text-window/application owners remain pending; tests do not claim native keyboard/mouse/device execution.

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: With no argument, including `$HOSTDIR()$`, return the selected directory name uppercased, or `<NONE>` when none is selected. The getter uppercases the stored name in place. With one argument, trim whitespace and uppercase it. Exact **OFF** clears the selection without attempting creation. Otherwise require at most 12 bytes, reject exact `.` and `..`, and reject any of `\ : * ? + / " , ; > < = [ ] |`. Interior spaces are accepted. Store the name and attempt to create `installation-root\name`; creation failure does not roll back selection. Successful setters return no text. Extra arguments or invalid names reject.
requirements.reason: Connected tests cover directory grammar, normalization and expansion order, clear, creation-failure persistence, recovery after rejection, and the 12/13-byte boundary in CP437 and UTF-8. SyncTERM stores named directories inside the per-BBS RIP cache.

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: A whitespace-only argument becomes empty and clears selection while attempting root-path creation. Empty parentheses are the getter, and `HOSTDIR("")` is a parser error. This variable has no explicit host-service-callback gate. Its clear keyword is **OFF**, whereas [`RIP_SWITCH_DIRECTORY`](6.2-asset-delivery-and-storage.md#rip_switch_directory) recognizes literal `$OFF$` before its own expansion stage. Parameter text in the variable is not a recursively evaluated expression; preprocessing can compose it before the dollar parser runs.

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: SEND always requires at least one filename. The shared parser limits each filename argument to 20 bytes and the whole list to 40 arguments (at most 37 filename arguments after the three keywords). RECEIVE protocols 0..4 also require one; RECEIVE protocols 5..8 do not require filenames and ignore any supplied filename arguments. Required filenames are joined with spaces and the `<>` block-mode terminator is appended. The handler invokes RIP_ENTER_BLOCK_MODE with decoded fields `(direction,protocol,type,0)` and that filename tail; this is the same transfer path and capability/refusal behavior, not a separate engine promising support for every keyword. Invalid keywords or missing required arguments reject. Empty comma fields do not supply a missing filename.
requirements.reason: Both directions accept 37 filename arguments after the three keywords and reject a 38th. The connected worker accepts 20 protocol bytes including converted CP437 and rejects 21. Native tests cover the keyword and tail matrix.

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: RIPtel 3.1’s shared handler rejects an empty prepared receive tail for codes 0–5. Thus the XFER parser accepts the three keywords in `$XFER(RECEIVE,YMODEM,NONE)$`, but the shared handler sends no request to the client. Providing a filename argument to this macro does not change the empty tail it builds for YMODEM. See the [request and client support matrix](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#transfer-protocols).

requirements.heading: $RESET(TV,name)$
requirements.text: Exactly two nonempty arguments are required after empty comma fields are omitted. The variable name must be shorter than 20 bytes, start with an alphabetic byte, and continue with alphanumeric bytes or underscores. Lookup checks memory first, then the persistent store. If absent, nothing happens. If present and unprotected, delete the matching record. A protected record prompts for confirmation: No retains it, Yes deletes it. The original dialog branch cancels specifically on the No response; no other response is separately rejected. Deletion does not reset text windows or all variables.

The generic name validator’s empty-string edge cannot turn a missing field into “delete all,” because that field is omitted by the parser.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: The reset text variable is a general purpose reset command. Without any parameters, the text variable adheres to the original 1.54 RIPscrip command which performs the exact same operations as a [RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows) command. Some parameters used with the reset command require additional parameters to further specify what section is to be reset (eg, if you specify "TW" to reset a text window, you need to specify what text window [data table](7.1-data-tables.md) entry is to be reset). The portable RESET validates the entire request before applying any selector. An invalid parameter is a syntax error. A valid selector that reaches an unresettable target, such as a protected entry or an empty stack, is a no-op.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: Each release permits subsequent input of that device under its other gates, including local focus, pointer enable, and [per-window ANSI keyboard mode](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#ansi-mode-2-keyboard-gating). It leaves ordinary hotkey enablement intact and generates no synthetic input or scene end. A mouse release does not restore a capture or hover membership canceled by the scene lock. A keyboard release starts with the focus state left by the lock. [HEADER scene gates](1.1-protocol-and-command-hierarchy.md#scene-input-gates) · [Mouse gesture lifetime](4.2-mouse-fields-and-pointer.md#hover-and-callback-context).
requirements.reason: RESET(KEYBOARD) releases only the scene keyboard gate. The per-window ANSI mode and mouse interaction continue according to their own state.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **Original RIPtel 3.1.** The PC Micro driver uses a common HEADER lock word. MCURSOR selects arrow and suppresses the pending arrow replacement at scene release, while the lock remains set. KEYBOARD checks argument count and leaves both the lock and pointer as they were. A subsequent NO_MORE releases the original lock. [Original captures](../research/issue-286-reset-input-lock.md#original-callbacks-and-captured-state).
requirements.reason: Original-driver differentiation of pointer and input-gate effects.

The following completed rules adopt the existing definition, first-use, protection and parser ownership contracts; [derivation, source hashes and independent vectors](../research/issue-148-live-tw-reset.md). requirements.heading: Live Text-Window Reset Contract

This is a forced reset even if the resulting geometry/font match the old definition; it does not use ordinary `w`'s identical-definition retention branch. It resets slot 0 itself, without selecting another slot or executing a CUR expression.

requirements.heading: Live Text-Window Reset Contract
requirements.text: **Queries and independent state:** a successful nonzero deletion discards that entry's fixed resident query. A protected or undefined no-op retains all existing target/query state. Live TW reset, including **TBL and ALL**, retains the **floating TW query**: it is shared state, not an entry attached to TW 0 or whichever window is current. Clear it with the separate `RESET(QUERY,TW,CUR)` directive; outer SOFT also has its explicitly documented floating-query deletion. A TBL keeps fixed queries on protected surviving entries, while resetting 0 and deleting other applied entries removes their fixed queries. No query is executed by these operations.

A numeric 0 reset does not independently change the current index; if another TW remains current, subsequent raw text uses that window's retained font/activation/modes.

requirements.text: A bare `$RESET(STYLE)$` or `$RESET(ENV)$` applies one CUR operation. Accept the selectors below in either family. Apply the [ordinary dollar argument rules](#argument-bytes-and-local-backslashes) first. Trim outer ASCII whitespace from each parsed selector and compare keywords case-insensitively. An unknown or out-of-range selector rejects the entire request as a variable syntax error. This follows the general rule in ALPHA 4 §5.9.1. requirements.heading: Live STYLE and ENV Reset Contract
requirements.text: **STYLE defaults and use.** Use the [fixed graphical style record](7.1-data-tables.md#initial-and-per-slot-defaults). When the reset reaches the selected style, subsequent drawing uses those defaults. Ordinary field setters still address the selected STYLE record, even if a numbered reset or TBL left it undefined. For example, with unprotected STYLE 5 selected, `$RESET(STYLE,5)$` followed by `c04` in palette mode sets its drawing color to index 4 while `INUSE(STYLE,5)` stays 0. `CUR(STYLE)` still returns 5. The next explicit selection of an undefined style uses the existing first-use initialization rule. [STYLE selection](7.1-data-tables.md#rip_switch_style).

requirements.heading: Live STYLE and ENV Reset Contract
requirements.text: **ENV defaults and activation.** The replacement record contains WORLD 640 × 350, Base Math 36, coordinate width 2, RGB precision 0 (palette mode), mouse pointer number 0 (arrow), and an inherited legacy character-set override. A noncurrent target receives stored defaults only. In the **portable profile**, any successful reset of the selected ENV installs the defaults in both the record and the active environment at the same logical step, including when a numbered reset or TBL clears the selected entry's definition. Subsequent commands use the new parser widths, radix, color mode and world conversion. Present the arrow through the ordinary pointer rules. Keep the shared SDCS fallback, connection encoding and ANSI window state under their own lifetime rules. Existing screen pixels, other table selections and the global input lock are retained. [ENV ownership](7.1-data-tables.md#environment-table).
requirements.reason: The active engine and bare queries use the selected record even when undefined. Connected fixtures cover next-command decoding, world, palette, pointer, input lock, ANSI state, numeric queries and backup preservation.

requirements.heading: Live STYLE and ENV Reset Contract

After a numbered reset of selected nonzero slot 5, `WORLD(5)` and `COLORMODE(5)` expand to `-1` because that entry is undefined. A following CUR reset of that slot makes the numbered queries return the defaults again.

requirements.heading: Other RESET Families
requirements.text: **Shipped palette lifecycle:** resetting an unprotected nonzero slot restores default RGB values and **clears its defined/in-use flag**. Resetting an already undefined unprotected slot leaves it undefined; it does not error or define it. A protected specific/current slot rejects unchanged; TBL and SOFT skip protected slots. HARD removes their protection and resets all nonzero slots to undefined. Slot zero remains defined and unprotectable. Reset preserves the current palette index, except HARD selects zero, so a selected palette can become undefined after a specific/TBL/SOFT reset. Reselecting it with `$CUR(PAL,n)$` defines it again. See the [palette lifecycle truth table](7.1-data-tables.md#palette-reset-lifecycle) and [original reset/status probes](../research/issue-16-table-lifecycle.md).
requirements.reason: Palette reset preserves protection and selection while clearing eligible nonzero in-use flags and restoring default colors.

requirements.heading: Other RESET Families
requirements.text: After selecting/modifying palette 5, `$RESET(PAL,5)$` yields `$INUSE(PAL,5)$` = `0`, `$ISPROT(PAL,5)$` = `-1`, and `$CUR(PAL)$` = `5`. Numeric ISPROT checks definition first; its separate CUR form directly tests current protection and returns `0` for this undefined-but-current unprotected slot.

requirements.heading: Other RESET Families
requirements.text: **PORT** - This variation on the reset command resets one or more ports in some way. The exact way that one is reset varies depending on the type of port specified. If no additional parameters are specified, then the current port is reset. Otherwise, you may reset a specific port number in the port data table, or one (or all) of the port data backup areas. If you reset a specific port in the port data table, what happens varies depending on what kind of port it is. If it is port #0 (which cannot be deleted), then the only thing that happens is that any resident queries for that port/viewport are deleted, the viewport is made full screen and the viewport is erased to the background color (in that order). If the port number (from 1-35) represents a screen port, then any resident query attached to that port/viewport is deleted and the port itself is deleted. If it is an offscreen port, then that port is also deleted (offscreen ports cannot have resident queries). In any event, if the port being deleted happens to be the current port, then the port is automatically switched to port #0 (the screen's port). The following parameters are permitted with this reset port). Whenever the current port is reset, the port is automatically switched to port #0. Beware of this when chaining multiple port resets together at the same time. For example, if port #5 is current and you issue the following command `$RESET(PORT, 5, CUR)$`, then port number 5 will be deleted, then it would switch back to port #0 which is the screen port and cannot be deleted, so only its viewport will be reset. The following parameters are permitted with this reset command to control what type of reset operation is to be performed:
requirements.reason: PORT resets validate all selectors, apply them in order and resolve CUR after deletion. Zero clears its fixed query and paints its full viewport with the active background. Protected records and independent saved copies survive applicable operations.

requirements.reason: Mouse backups are bound to actual sessions for simple fields and ordinary plain/clipboard/ICON button definitions. RESET(MOUSE) defaults to TBL; explicit selectors prevalidate and retain protected snapshots; field-only reset retains handlers. All failures remain below void parsing. requirements.text: **SCREEN** - When no parameters are specified, the entire video screen is cleared to color #0 (usually black). No viewports are modified, nor are any drawing ports, text windows, mouse fields or anything else. The following parameters are allowed, providing you with the ability to reset particular screen aspects:
requirements.reason: Connected screen-only SAVE/RESTORE and all numbered aliases capture physical PORT0 pixels plus current-palette RGB. Native ANSI ink and both blink planes are merged only for an explicit backup; raw graphics indexes and literal reset black are retained where unchanged, using the existing presentation image and console raster. Restore copies the unscaled physical overlap without resizing/replacing port identity, overwrites current PAL RGB even if protected/undefined, and leaves all selectors/flags/styles/TW/mouse/status metadata live. BASE is reusable, slots/protection/stack/COPY use owned manager snapshots; numeric RESTORE requests deletion even after failure while POP is success-dependent. Valid failed actions return no value or variable error and report only the private lower-level diagnostic; syntax preflight remains distinct. RESET(SCREEN) clears physical index 0; explicit backup selectors retain protected saves. Native and TCP vectors cover 5-to-17 palette binding, empty/undefined palette flags, no extra state, split bytes, failed capture/presentation, malformed aliases, both planes, circular native scroll/cursor retention, and nonfatal continuation. SAVEALL/RESTOREALL remain separate pending operations.

requirements.text: **VIEW** - When no parameters are specified, then the viewport of the current drawing port is reset to the full dimensions of the port itself, and activated. Other possible parameters allow you to modify other viewports of other ports. The possible parameters are:
requirements.reason: Connected RESET(VIEW) accepts implied/current, decimal0..35 and TBL, validates all selectors/bindings before effects, restores each writable defined port viewport to full port-relative bounds and activates it. Protected/undefined entries are no-ops; selection, pixels, cursor/image data, resident queries, clipboard and remembered DEVICE copy offsets remain intact. Native independent state/content/pair/query/unbound cases and actual CP437/UTF8 TCP captures cover inactive-vs-MVP, zero WORLD/radix independence, copy-pair reuse and physical sub-port origin/far-edge clipping. Earlier native PCB/connected SOFT evidence is reused for the separate full-reset pair rules; this does not accept HEADER or the other unfinished RESET families.

requirements.heading: Resident Query Reset
requirements.text: Apply the [ordinary dollar argument rules](#argument-bytes-and-local-backslashes), trim outer ASCII whitespace and compare keywords case-insensitively. A numeric selector is a decimal digit string in 0 through 35, independent of Base Math. A family-specific list starts with exactly one TW or VIEW. Use two separate RESET requests for two different individual family lists. `QUERY,ALL` is the complete two-family form. Validate the entire argument list before deletion. For example, `$RESET(QUERY,TW,5,VIEW,CUR)$` and `$RESET(QUERY,TW,5,36)$` are syntax errors that leave all expressions intact.
requirements.reason: QUERY resets validate before effects and clear floating or eligible fixed live expressions in the documented order. Native tests inspect stored expressions directly. Connected tests check recovery, unchanged pixels and live hover behavior.

requirements.heading: Resident Query Reset
requirements.text: A fixed expression is eligible on a defined unprotected TW or a defined unprotected screen port. Protected entries retain their fixed expressions. An undefined slot, an offscreen port or an absent expression is a no-op and later selectors still run. Changing a floating expression requires no numbered-entry test. This reset affects live expression storage only. It preserves definitions, selection, activation, pixels, backups and mouse-field hover expressions. It executes no stored expression and expands to no text.

requirements.heading: $OFF$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$OFF$` **Syntax:** `$OFF$`

requirements.heading: $OFF$
requirements.text: `$OFF$` is not a mode toggle but a sentinel value: sent as the text of a deferred query ([RIP_QUERY](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_query) modes 1/2) it _cancels_ the stored deferred command, and 2.00a4 uses it likewise to disable refresh expressions ([RIP_SET_REFRESH](5.0-host-commands.md#rip_set_refresh) with `$OFF$` - see [`$NOREFRESH$`](#norefresh)).
requirements.reason: Level-2 R validates four reserved digits in the current radix and stores the deferred expression. The connected local action and REFRESH send a separate late expansion, and NOREFRESH, OFF, empty definition, SOFT, HARD and header flag 16 clear it. Shared host expansion covers controls, variables, prompts and delays. Pick lists remain tracked separately.

requirements.text: _Return the client's fixed character-set name_

requirements.heading: $CDCS$
requirements.text: `$CDCS$` or `$CDCS()$` expands to ASCII `USASCII`. Reject any parsed argument.

requirements.heading: $CHARSET$
requirements.text: _Query effective legacy character-set metadata_
requirements.reason: Capability heading or fixture framing.

requirements.heading: $CHARSET$
requirements.text: `$CHARSET$`, `$CHARSET()$` and `$CHARSET(CUR)$` query the current ENV. `$CHARSET(env)$` selects ENV 0–35 by unsigned decimal number. A defined ENV explicitly set to `USASCII` or `KANJI` returns that name. Otherwise return `KANJI` if the shared [SDCS fallback](#sdcs) is KANJI, or `USASCII` if that fallback is USASCII or off. A valid but undefined ENV number returns the two ASCII bytes `-1`. The provider only reads metadata.

requirements.heading: $DCS$
requirements.text: _Query or set a stored ENV character-set override_
requirements.reason: Capability heading or fixture framing.

requirements.heading: $DCS$
requirements.text: `$DCS$` and `$DCS()$` query the current ENV. `$DCS(env)$` queries another ENV or accepts `CUR` for the current ENV. `$DCS(env,selector)$` takes `QUERY`, `USASCII`, `KANJI` or `OFF`. A single argument is always the ENV selector, so use `$DCS(CUR,KANJI)$` for a current-ENV setter.

requirements.heading: $DCS$
requirements.text: `QUERY` returns the stored override `USASCII` or `KANJI`, or ASCII `0` for an inherited value. For a valid but undefined ENV the provider returns `-1` without creating a record, including in the two-argument form. For a defined ENV the two name setters store an explicit override even on a protected ENV. `OFF` clears the override to inherited on a protected ENV and leaves an unprotected ENV's override in place. Each accepted setter on a defined ENV expands to an empty string. To clear the override on an unprotected ENV, use `$RESET(CHARSET,DCS,env)$` with a defined target. That reset selector also accepts `CUR` or `TBL` and preserves protected overrides.

requirements.heading: $LANG$
requirements.text: _Return the client's fixed language name_

requirements.heading: $LANG$
requirements.text: `$LANG$`, `$LANG()$` and `$LANG(THREECHAR)$` expand to `eng`. `$LANG(TWOCHAR)$` expands to `en` and `$LANG(VERBOSE)$` expands to `English`. These values are ASCII and independent of ENV selection, any locale or connection encoding. Reject other selectors or excess parsed arguments.

requirements.heading: $SDCS$
requirements.text: _Query or set shared legacy character-set metadata_
requirements.reason: Capability heading or fixture framing.

requirements.heading: $SDCS$
requirements.text: `$SDCS$`, `$SDCS()$` and `$SDCS(QUERY)$` return `USASCII`, `KANJI` or ASCII `-1` for off. The single setters `$SDCS(USASCII)$`, `$SDCS(KANJI)$` and `$SDCS(OFF)$` set that fallback and expand to an empty string. `$RESET(CHARSET,SDCS,CUR)$` also sets it to off. While off, an inherited ENV's `CHARSET` response is `USASCII`.

requirements.heading: $SDCS$
requirements.text: The five providers match keywords case-insensitively and use ordinary [parsed argument and rejection rules](5.2-templates-and-conditionals.md#eligible-providers-and-rejected-codes). In CHARSET and DCS, a malformed ENV selector or number outside 0–35 rejects the reference. A defined target with an unknown DCS selector also rejects. An ENV selector identifies the [environment table](7.1-data-tables.md#environment-table) independently of the active text-window index.

requirements.heading: Character-set Metadata Lifetime and Example
requirements.text: RIPtel 3.1 initializes the fallback to USASCII and every fresh ENV's override to inherited. First selection of an unused ENV gives it the default inherited record. ANSI controls and creation, selection or reset of a text window use their [own state](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#byte-character-sets-in-riptel-31). ENV selection changes which override CUR reads. SENV/RENV capture and restore the per-entry overrides with the records. The shared fallback remains live across both operations.

requirements.heading: Character-set Metadata Lifetime and Example
requirements.text: The ordinary drawing/SOFT reset defaults unprotected ENV records to inherited and selects ENV 0. Protected overrides survive. The completed HARD reset defaults all ENV overrides to inherited. Both resets preserve the shared fallback. For the portable RIPtel profile, implement these variables as metadata and use a separately chosen connection encoding. requirements.heading: $CLS$
requirements.text: Takes zero arguments and expands to no text. Any supplied argument is a recognized-macro evaluation error. A valid call replaces every backing pixel of the physical RIP screen (PORT0) with literal RGB `(0,0,0)`. The fill covers the entire DEVICE extent, independent of the current drawing port, viewport rectangles or activation, current write mode, WORLD mapping, palette index 0 and STYLE background. An indexed implementation must realize the black fill even with a nonblack index 0.
requirements.reason: Connected fixed RGB-black physical fill and retained session state under PR #203.

requirements.heading: $CLS$
requirements.text: CLS erases visible screen pixels, including the pixels previously drawn by ANSI text, without resetting the terminal. Keep current port and text-window selections, dimensions and activation, the live and saved ANSI cursors, rendition and parser state, drawing and palette state, offscreen bitmaps, field definitions and saved backups. The [status-bar option](#status-bar-state-and-presentation) and the logical visibility of the caret are retained. The terminal may suspend those overlays while presenting the cleared canvas.

The 3.0 profile adopts the fixed-black screen effect of that call. [Original registration, brush and rectangle trace](../research/issue-200-cls-black.md).

requirements.heading: $COLORMODE$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$COLORMODE(env_no, mode, bits)$`
requirements.reason: Reconciled with adopted PR #56/#57 macro contract. COLORMODE accepts/reports 1..8, sets only an already-defined ENV record, bypasses its protection and preserves selection/other records; undefined getters reply -1 without defining or diagnosing. All existing foreground/fill/background/text/curve/path consumers use actual precision. Packed N-bit blue/green/red components normalize to RGB8 with nearest full-range rounding, then use the existing declared 256-color current-palette match. CM input is UltraNum in every nonzero precision independently of Base Math; unused high bits of the 24-bit code do not enter component masks. Native independent packed-code/RGB literals cover every precision and both radices, protected current/noncurrent macros, undefined/error paths, rendering and erase. Real CP437/UTF-8 sessions on five entry rasters draw green points, blue fills and red erasures at all eight precisions, check macro/wire distinction, protected STYLE independence and invalid-input recovery. This does not claim truecolor-surface support, unimplemented CM command families or complete ENV context switching.

It responds with a number that indicates whether or not the terminal is in direct RGB encoding mode or if it is in color palette mapping mode. If the value is 0, then it is palette mapping mode. The [logical RIP palette](2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#palette-mapping-and-direct-rgb-mode) can be implemented on an RGB framebuffer. requirements.heading: $PALENTRY$
requirements.text: This variable returns one or more RGB values stored in one of the drawing color palettes. The `<pal>` parameter determines which palette in the palette data table is to be inquired about, and its value can be from 0-35 to explicitly reference a specific color palette number, or it can be CUR to indicate the current color palette.
requirements.reason: The native test checks required arguments, selector limits and CUR, inclusive ranges, ALL, malformed references and capacity boundaries. Live RIP_QUERY checks the complete ALL result, specific entries, and undefined palettes after a reset.

requirements.heading: $PALENTRY$
requirements.text: The `<start>` parameter must be specified, and indicates which palette entry in the palette is to be inquired about. If the `<stop>` parameter is omitted, then only one entry will be queried, the `<start>` entry. If `<stop>` is supplied, then it must be equal to or greater than `<start>` (not to exceed 255). So if `<start>` is 5 and `<stop>` is 7 then three palette entries will be inquired about, starting with entry #5.
requirements.reason: The native test checks required arguments, selector limits and CUR, inclusive ranges, ALL, malformed references and capacity boundaries. Live RIP_QUERY checks the complete ALL result, specific entries, and undefined palettes after a reset.

requirements.reason: PALENTRY reports the stored six bits of every component as inclusive, ordered RGB triples prefixed by 6;. Connected and native tests cover exact single, range and undefined replies.

requirements.heading: $PALENTRY$
requirements.text: RIPtel 3.1 prefixes a defined palette result with ASCII `6;`. The triples are **stored six-bit decimal components**, each in 0–63. A range result lists ascending entries and separates the triples with commas. It contains no trailing comma or line ending. The value is substituted into the enclosing HCL text.
requirements.reason: PALENTRY reports the stored six bits of every component as inclusive, ordered RGB triples prefixed by 6;. Connected and native tests cover exact single, range and undefined replies.

requirements.heading: $PALENTRY$
requirements.text: For example, after an accepted `D` or `d` write of RGB (18,52,86) to index 32 in the current defined palette, `$PALENTRY(CUR,32)$` substitutes `6;4:13:21`. The result is the same before and after reselecting that palette. An entry stored as white returns `6;63:63:63`. A stored `Q` prefix is visible here even when a later invalid master color prevented publication. [Master-color update order](2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_palette). `$PALENTRY(CUR,ALL)$` returns all 256 stored triples with a single `6;` prefix. Current direct-RGB precision and display palette requests do not enter this query. See the [storage and publication rule](2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#stored-color-and-palette-publication).
requirements.reason: Live RIPv3 master-color edits implement the adopted PR #276 collection, storage and publication rules.

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: The source port owns the [optional remembered pair](7.0-drawing-ports.md#remembered-copy-pairs) established by the listed producer operations. If it is `P=(Rs,Rd)`, PCB reads **current source viewport origin + Rd** and writes **current destination viewport origin + Rs**, in DEVICE units. Stored offsets are already projected and logically viewport-trimmed; WORLD changes do not reinterpret them. [Physical storage/sample clipping](7.0-drawing-ports.md#physical-storage-and-sample-coverage) does not shrink/round the pair or refit its mapping, and a successful logically nonempty transfer publishes even when physical sampling writes nothing. Viewport movement changes their absolute origins and current viewport extents still clip the new transfer. The original source port number is not a permanent destination binding: paste goes into whatever port is current now.

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: **Portable profile.** Count arguments after the ordinary [dollar-call argument decoding](#argument-bytes-and-local-backslashes). With zero arguments, delete all live simple mouse fields and mouse-active buttons, as with [RIP_KILL_MOUSE_FIELDS](4.2-mouse-fields-and-pointer.md#rip_kill_mouse_fields). The selective form takes four decimal WORLD coordinates and an optional selector. Each coordinate is an ASCII digit string with a value from 0 through 65535, independent of Base Math. The selector is ASCII case-insensitive `IN` or `OUT`, with `IN` as the default. Reject any other argument count, invalid coordinate or unknown selector as a variable evaluation error before deleting fields or clearing focus.

requirements.heading: $SMF$

This is designed especially for the graphical designer who wishes to pop-up a dialog box on the screen with one or more mouse fields, and when finished, to restore the screen and original mouse fields. requirements.heading: $BACKSTAT$
requirements.text: The "base" field is set to "0" if the base save area is not in use, or "1" if it is in use. The "stack" field is set to the number of entries that are currently saved on the stack ("0" if its empty). The "slots" field states how many entries are saved in the data save slots. The "free" field determines how many stack/slot areas are not in use (ie, how many more can hold data). The final ten entries "s0" through "s9" are set to "0" or "1" indicating if that specific data save slot is currently in use or not. If you add up the "stack" and "slots" value, you will get a total value of entries stored in the stack/slot system. If you add this total value up with the value of "free", then you get the maximum number of entries allowed to be saved in the stack/slot system (currently this should be set not exceed 10).

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: When you are referring to a copy operation that involves the entire data table, you use the keyword "TBL". When referring to the Base Data Save Area, the keyword "BASE" is used. A Data Save Slot number is specified with the letter "S" followed by the slot index number (eg, S0, S3, S5, etc). An actual data table entry number is specified simply as an actual number from 0 to the total number of entries in the data table minus one. _(v2.A3)_
requirements.reason: COPY resolves base, numbered and stack locations in the shared backup service. Live entry copies dispatch by family. Whole-table and entry fixtures check source lifetime, eligibility and destination order.

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: Destinations for entire data tables can be the BASE save area, a Data Save Slot (S0-S9) or you can PUSH it onto the stack. _(v2.A4)_
requirements.reason: COPY resolves base, numbered and stack locations in the shared backup service. Live entry copies dispatch by family. Whole-table and entry fixtures check source lifetime, eligibility and destination order.

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: You can also specify the source as POP to indicate that you are copying (popping) data from the stack to some other destination (TBL, BASE or S0-S9). If you specify only one destination location, then the contents of the stack are copied to that location, then the stack is "popped", which basically deletes the top item on the stack (the one that was just copied). If you have multiple destinations, then the stack item is copied to each of those locations, then it is finally deleted from the stack after all of the copy operations are complete. _(v2.A4)_
requirements.reason: COPY resolves base, numbered and stack locations in the shared backup service. Live entry copies dispatch by family. Whole-table and entry fixtures check source lifetime, eligibility and destination order.

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: Our of all six data tables that have 36 separate entries, one of them doesn't permit direct copying from one entry to another within the same data table. That table is the drawing port table. The reason for this is because of how complicated the subject of performing port copying from one entry to another. Do you copy over just the graphical data, and if so, do you stretch it to fit in the destination port if the dimensions of the ports don't match? On the other hand do you duplicate the port definition entirely, potentially copying over the bitmap data? If so, how do you handle copying to port #0 which cannot be deleted or re-defined? With all of these complicated issues involved, it was decided not to allow for ports to be copied from one entry to another. Perhaps in the future we will allow for this kind of operation when more research on the issues can be performed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.text: **BUT selection versus definition:** A specific/table BUT reset retains its selected index even if that slot becomes undefined. Successful `1B` then marks that current slot in use, so a later `$CUR(BUT,n)$` retains the newly written style. Selection defaults only a still-undefined destination, also clearing any surviving protection in the already adopted inconsistent metadata case. Query-only `$CUR(BUT)$` has no defining side effect. requirements.heading: $ISPROT$
requirements.text: This command returns a value indicating if the specified element in the desired data object is protected or not. If it is protected, then it returns a "1". "0" is returned if it is not protected. For an individual numbered live entry or numbered backup slot, a missing element returns `-1`. ALL and ANY always return Boolean digits. ALL requires every live entry 1–35 to be defined and protected. ANY requires at least one defined and protected entry. Undefined and unprotected entries fail the per-entry predicate; entry 0 is excluded. Use the [backup aggregate predicates](#backup-query-aggregates) for ALLSLOTS and ANYSLOTS. The shipped CUR branch directly tests current protection without this definition check; an undefined-but-current palette after reset can therefore return "0" through CUR while its numeric ISPROT query returns "-1" ([native derivation](../research/issue-16-table-lifecycle.md)). requirements.reason: For each of TW, PORT, BUT, STYLE, PAL and ENV, a connected session checks ANY and ALL with no protected entries, 34 protected entries and slot 35 absent, all defined with slot 35 unprotected, and every nonzero slot protected. UNPROT(ALL) returns both aggregate queries to zero.

requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: _Query or replace a drawing port’s image rectangle and JPEG flags_
requirements.reason: Evidence, heading, sample input or explanatory navigation for the adjacent contract.

requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: **Query:** `$IMGSTYLE$` or `$IMGSTYLE(port)$`
requirements.reason: The separate IMGSTYLE callback supports bare/current/named queries and decimal setters for screen/offscreen ports. Keywords are case-insensitive OR values, including duplicates; no keywords replaces flags with zero. Undefined/inactive targets return -1 without mutation/diagnostic; protected enabled targets query successfully and setters return no value without mutation/error. Valid setters temporarily select the target and restore the previous selection even on conversion failure. Queries convert the complete stored device boundaries through the live current WORLD, without subtracting the far increment. Independent literal replies, all keyword combinations, invalid parameters, state/selection recovery and every supported canvas are tested. Enclosing multi-action host expansion is a separate acceptance requirement.

requirements.reason: The separate IMGSTYLE callback supports bare/current/named queries and decimal setters for screen/offscreen ports. requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: `port` is decimal 0..35 or case-insensitive CUR; omitted in the query means current. CUR may identify a screen **or offscreen** port. The setter temporarily selects the target, invokes [RIP_IMAGE_STYLE](4.1-jpeg-images.md#rip_image_style), then restores the previous current port. Coordinates are decimal values in the current world frame.

requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: The optional trailing keywords are case-insensitive, may repeat, and are OR’d together: **ASPECT=1, DELETE=2, NOCLEAR=4, USEPAL=8**. These replace the target’s flags. **Omitting all keywords sets flags to zero**, rather than retaining prior flags; there is no numeric-flags argument. Unknown keywords, a selector outside 0..35/CUR, nonnumeric coordinates or a set form with fewer than four coordinates cause a variable error without changing image state. Wallpaper bits 16/32 have no IMGSTYLE keyword in this driver. HCL [bitmap playback](5.3-local-playback.md#which-image-style-flags-apply) uses the stored rectangle but ignores every image-style flag; the flag effects below are JPEG-specific. DELETE is stored but has no JPEG deletion effect; see the [flag table](4.1-jpeg-images.md#rip_image_style).

Independent literal replies, all keyword combinations, invalid parameters, state/selection recovery and every supported canvas are tested. Enclosing multi-action host expansion is a separate acceptance requirement. Live bitmap tests cover geometry sharing and independent flag behavior.

requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: For an undefined target or a target with its viewport disabled, query **and set** return **`-1`**, leave state unchanged and do not set variable error. They do not create a port. A protected enabled target can be queried; its setter returns no value, leaves state unchanged and does not set variable error. A successful setter also returns no value. The [ordinary expansion policy](5.2-templates-and-conditionals.md) for a no-value action is separate from the callback’s state effects.

Independent literal replies, all keyword combinations, invalid parameters, state/selection recovery and every supported canvas are tested. requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: A successful query returns five unpadded decimal fields separated by colons: **`x0:y0:x1:y1:flags`**, with no added spaces or line ending. The original callback converts stored device rectangle boundaries back to world coordinates and **does not subtract the setter’s far-edge +1**. For example, at 1280×960 world / 640×480 device, setting (20,40,220,240) with ASPECT and NOCLEAR gives query **`20:40:222:242:5`**, not the original last two input coordinates. Do not use this query as a lossless round trip of the setter’s input.

requirements.text: _Navigate column-system overflow pages_

requirements.heading: $OVERFLOW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$OVERFLOW([article [,operation [,mode]]])$`
requirements.reason: Connected CP437 and UTF-8 exercise source and remainder replay, the live pager field, boundary abort, page-state lifetime and cache cleanup. Native RIP3 session tests verify navigation modes, verbose boundary messages and signed-word page assignment.

requirements.heading: $OVERFLOW$
requirements.text: The [column-system contract](3.1-column-text-system.md#pagination---overflow-and-resetoverflow) defines the complete argument and state table. Article is decimal 1..35 or CUR; omitted means selected article. Omitted operation or CUR returns an opaque saved-page filename (or `<NONE>`); PAGE returns the one-based display number. NEXT/PREV modify a zero-based current index and return an empty string on success. Their SETVERBOSE mode additionally notifies at a boundary, which aborts the surrounding evaluation before a following playback macro. QUERY is non-mutating; the shipped PREV,QUERY defect returns the filename for current+1. Numeric operation selects an already available zero-based index; RESET disables and clears one article’s paging state while retaining its column definitions. Global [`$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`](#reset) also removes all columns and selection. Overflow pages are generated lazily when text is rendered, not precomputed as a total page list.
requirements.reason: Connected CP437 and UTF-8 exercise source and remainder replay, the live pager field, boundary abort, page-state lifetime and cache cleanup. Native RIP3 session tests verify navigation modes, verbose boundary messages and signed-word page assignment.

requirements.heading: 5.2 Templates & Conditionals
requirements.text: Templates - the Host Command Language's mechanism for _building_ [host commands](5.0-host-commands.md) out of pieces, which the White Paper calls "a cookie-cutter approach to host commands," constructed from whichever buttons are selected and which are not. requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: The driver has two stages with different rescan rules. Preprocessing handles angle macros/conditionals; ordinary expansion handles dollar variables, slot embedding and enabled host directives. The number of ordinary passes depends on the consumer.
requirements.reason: Connected text skips a second ordinary expansion. The computed mouse-field action resolves a name in the angle pass and invokes the resulting playback in the host passes.

requirements.text: | `RIP_TEXT_METRIC` | Preprocess, then one ordinary pass permitting data callbacks but no direct user-variable fallback; `<<NAME>>` can still supply a user value during preprocessing |

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: | Host-command execution | Preprocess the host-command string, split/handle command blocks and templates, then make exactly two ordinary passes on each resulting response before transmission |
requirements.reason: The host and graphical preprocessors use the same angle and conditional workers. The parser and reducer fixtures cover quoting, branch/provider order and rejection. Live queries, text and JPEG names exercise expansion and recovery.

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: A button's third payload slot is [stored host source](4.3-buttons.md#creation-and-deferred-host-validation), not an ordinary graphical-text argument evaluated at definition. Its pure preflight does not run this host pipeline or reject a suffix that the established execution stages never reach. The separate filename/label slots keep their normal rendering consumers.
requirements.reason: The slideshow button stores its host source without running assignments or playback at definition. Native and connected tests distinguish a clipped suffix from reached processing.

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: Graphical filename, label, T/@ and metric arguments have the [consumer-specific permission, byte and continuation contract](#graphical-consumer-expansion). Host execution additionally enables active-only callbacks, ordinary slot embedding, playback and control decoding. Descriptive Value/Active labels are not permission masks: some mixed setters are callable in graphical contexts and others are not. A newly inserted dollar result does not restart the angle stage.
requirements.reason: Filename and label callbacks select state at definition while the stored host action changes the slide only on click. The graphical worker retains disabled playback and slot references.

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: The four local playback prefixes have a later [shared filename transformation](5.3-local-playback.md#shared-filename-contract): dollar quoting/20-byte parsing, ASCII uppercase, state substitutions and media extension/lookup. This is not another angle or ordinary expansion pass; valid enabled tokens produce empty replacement text.
requirements.reason: The host and graphical preprocessors use the same angle and conditional workers. The parser and reducer fixtures cover quoting, branch/provider order and rejection. Live queries, text and JPEG names exercise expansion and recovery.

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: Pick lists are enabled in **both ordinary HCL passes**: the first-pass mask defers controls/backslashes, not modal selection. Their [complete parser/pass profile](5.4-popup-lists.md#ordinary-passes-and-transmission) splices a selected original response and skips it in that pass; there is no fresh recursion or early response-prefix transmission. Pass-two selections receive no third pass.
requirements.reason: Both ordinary passes recognize pick lists and retain the selected raw span until the proper scan stage. Native and live vectors verify deferred template/variable insertion and final-response ordering.

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: Within **one ordinary pass**, scan from left to right. A successful variable or `$?N$` expansion replaces the reference and continues **after the inserted text**, so new codes in that insertion are not evaluated during the same pass. Active variables can perform an action and insert no text. A known built-in rejected for invalid arguments does not become a user-variable lookup. The [overflow boundary abort](3.1-column-text-system.md#pagination---overflow-and-resetoverflow) stops ordinary expansion before following codes in that pass.
requirements.reason: Owned 36-slot template storage and immediate host block processing implement [] direct blocks, [N:] raw ordinary definitions and [ABC] list-order chaining before exactly two ordinary passes per response. Every $?$ uses intended insertion rather than the native unsafe wrong-buffer offset. Marker-free templates discard the feed before callbacks execute; raw chain composition truncates at 4096 bytes and validates 1..36 indexes. Independent native vectors cover repeated/multiple markers, 36/37 levels, mixed/case-folded MegaNum slots, source-order replacement, discarded D/assignment effects, ESC/backslash segmentation, CP437/UTF-8 bytes, owned suspended source, allocation failures and recovery on all canvases. Required-empty lookup has a selection callback and aborts the host program; A later milestone verifies $?N$ embedding and PR95 response/storage clipping; actual radio/check-box button aggregation/highlighting, angle preprocessing and application routing remain separate pending work. This broader consumer or button/UI clause remains pending.

requirements.heading: Shipped Processing Order
requirements.text: For host responses, the first ordinary pass defers control-character decoding and backslash processing; the second uses the full caller feature set. requirements.text: Count bytes, excluding storage NUL, not Unicode characters or eventual glyphs. For each raw argument, template or provider value, use its prefix before the first NUL; discard bytes after that NUL **in that input/value**.
